1040.title: Custom fonts can be installed on Apple devices with iOS 13 and iPad OS.
1040.summary: Apple is offering users the custom font installation feature, introduced at the WWDC 2019 event this past June, with iOS 13 and iPad OS. Known for its closed ecosystem, Apple previously had no official way to install fonts on mobile operating systems. As a result of Apple’s collaboration with companies like Adobe,…
1040.content:
Apple is offering users the custom font installation feature, introduced at the [WWDC 2019](https://youtu.be/psL_5RIBqnY?t=4226) event this past June, with iOS 13 and iPad OS. Known for its closed ecosystem, Apple previously had no official way to install fonts on mobile operating systems. As a result of Apple’s collaboration with companies like [Adobe](https://www.adobe.com/tr/), [Monotype](https://www.monotype.com), and [DynaFont](https://www.dynacw.com/en/netshop/netshop.aspx), system-level font installation is now officially supported on phones and tablet devices. To use this feature, font providers or type foundries need to build an app or embed this functionality into an existing app.

One of the first apps to support the new font installation feature is [Font Diner](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/font-diner/id1480286620). Currently allowing you to install a free bundle of fonts for personal use only, the app offers a good and easy way to try out the font installation feature. Fonts installed with user consent are located under the **Settings → General → Fonts** menu. The alphabetical list of fonts, file size, and copyright information can be seen under this menu. Additionally, you can remove the font from the system without needing the installed app. It should be kept in mind that uninstalling a font installation app will also remove all fonts that came with the app. It is also worth noting that custom fonts being installed with this new method will not automatically be available in every app that uses system fonts. For this, apps that allow the use of custom fonts need to be selected. In the future, most apps may implement this, but you may need to wait for future app updates for custom fonts to appear as an option in the font menu of specific applications. Users who wish to try this feature can check out Apple’s built-in app *Pages*, which already supports custom font installation. (Source: [Typography.Guru](http://Typography.Guru))

> You can watch the relevant segment of the WWDC 2019 event where the font installation feature was introduced [here](https://youtu.be/psL_5RIBqnY?t=4226).

1061.title: Adobe ends Type 1 support.
1061.summary: Adobe announced that it will end support for Type 1 fonts in 2021. As a result, fonts in Type 1 format will no longer be listed in Photoshop’s font menu. Introduced in 1984 alongside PostScript and Apple LaserWriter, the Type 1 font format was superseded in 2000 by OpenType (opentype) fonts, which retained all the…
1061.content:
Adobe [announced](https://adobe.ly/2kbCCDY) that it will end support for Type 1 fonts in 2021. As a result, fonts in [Type 1](https://www.prepressure.com/fonts/basics/type1) format will no longer be listed in Photoshop’s font menu. Introduced in 1984 alongside [PostScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PostScript) and [Apple LaserWriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaserWriter), the Type 1 font format was superseded in 2000 by OpenType ([opentype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenType)) fonts, which retained all the advantages of Type 1 while offering cross-platform compatibility and advanced typographic features.

1067.title: Wim Crouwel has passed away.
1067.summary: Iconic graphic designer and typographer Wim Crouwel has passed away in his native Amsterdam at the age of 90. Born in the Netherlands in 1928, Crouwel studied at Academie Minerva in Groningen, Netherlands, between 1947 and 1949. He began his career in 1955 designing exhibitions, graphics, and products together with…
1067.content:
Iconic graphic designer and typographer [Wim Crouwel](http://www.iconofgraphics.com/Wim-Crouwel/) has [passed away](http://bit.ly/2mmK67G) in his native Amsterdam at the age of 90.

Born in the Netherlands in 1928, Crouwel studied at Academie Minerva in Groningen, Netherlands, between 1947 and 1949. He began his career in 1955 designing exhibitions, graphics, and products together with Kho Liang Ie. In 1963, he became one of the founders of the design studio [Total Design](https://www.totaldesign.com). In 1967, he designed the typeface New Alphabet. In 1970, he designed the Netherlands pavilion for Expo '70 in Osaka. In addition to graphic design, he was actively involved in education. Crouwel’s work is especially recognized for its grid-based layout and use of typography in the [International Typographic Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Typographic_Style).

1187.title: GMK 38th Graphic Design Awards find their winners.
1187.summary: The 38th Graphic Design Exhibition, organized since 1981 by the Turkish Society of Graphic Designers (GMK), opened on Friday, November 1, 2019, at the Tophane-i Amire Culture and Arts Center. In the competition, where 236 graphic designers submitted 676 works, Best and Achievement Awards were presented across 26…
1187.content:
The 38th Graphic Design Exhibition, organized since 1981 by the [Turkish Society of Graphic Designers](http://gmk.org.tr) (GMK), [opened](http://gmk.org.tr/news/gmkdan/38-grafik-tasarim-odulleri-sahiplerini-buldu) on Friday, November 1, 2019, at the Tophane-i Amire Culture and Arts Center. In the competition, where 236 graphic designers submitted 676 works, Best and Achievement Awards were presented across 26 categories, along with 7 special awards.

In the Typeface Design Category, the Best Award was presented to [Erman Yılmaz](http://ermanyilmaz.com) for his typeface [Gaslamp](http://ermanyilmaz.com/portfolio/gaslmap-typeface/); and Achievement Awards were given to [Fatih Hardal](http://fatihhardal.com) for his designs [Ampersand](https://www.behance.net/gallery/79726267/Ampersand-Typeface) and [Quad](https://www.behance.net/gallery/72967269/Quad-Typeface-(2018)), to Onur Aşkın for his design Le Corbusier, and to [Oğuzhan Cengiz](https://www.behance.net/oguzhancengiz) for his designs [Apron](https://www.behance.net/gallery/77601947/Apron-Font-Family) and [Grosen](https://www.behance.net/gallery/82795717/Grosen-Type-Family).

We congratulate our award-winning designers and wish them continued success.

1087.title: In-house norms used by Aldus Manutius
1087.summary: Hyphen Press is offering the book Type Spaces by Peter Burnhill, who passed away in 2007, for free to its readers. In his book, Peter Burnhill closely examines certain books from the early sixteenth century, gathering evidence of a rational measurement system based on features of these editions such as character…
1087.content:
[Hyphen Press](https://hyphenpress.co.uk/) is offering the book [Type Spaces](http://bit.ly/2JmJXfx) by Peter Burnhill, who passed away in 2007, for free to its readers.

In his book, Peter Burnhill closely examines certain books from the early sixteenth century, gathering evidence of a rational measurement system based on features of these editions such as character count, line length, and type area. According to him, [Aldus Manutius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldus_Manutius) and [Francesco Griffo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francesco_Griffo) used a series of in-house norms that could still be applied today.

1118.title: “How Aldus Manutius Saved Civilization?”
1118.summary: Image/Video: Video Source G. Scott Clemons’s 2015 talk on Aldus Manutius at a Type@Cooper event: “How Aldus Manutius Saved Civilization?” (Eng.) Clemons argues that Aldus’s striking decision at the end of the 15th century to abandon a scholarly life led out of love for literature and books and move to Venice, plunging…
1118.content:
*Image/Video: [Video Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aui8IXBVoGY&fbclid=IwAR3H5KCZc4V_ZZtfPji_FZgb_5ntULD27H_mK0GRLRUzdhIhwL0KUxAPXiw)*

G. Scott Clemons’s 2015 talk on Aldus Manutius at a [Type@Cooper](http://coopertype.org) event: [“How Aldus Manutius Saved Civilization?”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aui8IXBVoGY&fbclid=IwAR3H5KCZc4V_ZZtfPji_FZgb_5ntULD27H_mK0GRLRUzdhIhwL0KUxAPXiw) (Eng.)

Clemons argues that Aldus’s striking decision at the end of the 15th century to abandon a scholarly life led out of love for literature and books and move to Venice, plunging into the cutthroat trade of the printing world, continues to reverberate across modern fields such as textual criticism, book design, typography, book production, copyright law, collecting, and classical philology.

Clemons’s choice of talk title is also significant. He emphasizes that Aldus’s decision helped bring the Greek canon into the present day by printing ancient Greek works with movable type, thereby committing the surviving works to print for the first time.

> We also recommend reading on our [Medium](https://medium.com/tipografi) page the translated article titled [Typefaces as History: Aldus Manutius and the Noble Bembo](https://medium.com/tipografi/tarih-olarak-yazıyüzleri-aldus-manutius-ve-asil-bembo-a03ef4e89c0c?fbclid=IwAR1CEUazQInxiZZuGMBhXCGdu7rs4hoCRiEs0NUA49nbGh9afpU4kH-9CUU).

1512.title: Germany will remove Nazi traces from the phonetic alphabet.
1512.summary: According to a BBC report, Germany will update its phonetic alphabet due to additions made by the Nazis. Jewish names in the German phonetic alphabet—such as “David” for the letter “D”, “Nathan” for “N”, and “Zacharias” (Zechariah) for “Z”—were replaced during the Nazi regime that ruled between 1933 and 1945. Now,…
1512.content:
[According to a BBC report,](https://www.bbc.com/turkce/haberler-dunya-55187680) Germany will update its phonetic alphabet due to additions made by the Nazis. Jewish names in the German phonetic alphabet—such as “David” for the letter “D”, “Nathan” for “N”, and “Zacharias” (Zechariah) for “Z”—were replaced during the Nazi regime that ruled between 1933 and 1945. Now, experts affiliated with the German Institute for Standardization (DIN) are working on a new phonetic alphabet to be announced to the public in 2022.

Following Benguiat’s passing, Steven Heller penned an article titled The Benguiat Period, expressing his admiration…
1578.content:
American type designer [Ed Benguiat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Benguiat), who created more than 600 typefaces including Tiffany, Bookman, Panache, Souvenir, as well as Benguiat and Benguiat Gothic bearing his own surname, has passed away.

Following Benguiat’s passing, Steven Heller penned an article titled [The Benguiat Period](https://www.printmag.com/post/the-daily-heller-the-benguiat-period), expressing his admiration for Benguiat. The Type Directors Club re-shared the video recordings of their [interview](https://youtu.be/KHjdoSP-jVc) with Benguiat conducted in 2016 as part of the *Legends of Typography* series and the [interview](https://vimeo.com/225122829) conducted by Debbie Millman in 2017. Neil Genzlinger paid tribute to Benguiat, who redesigned The New York Times logo, with an [article](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/10/16/business/media/ed-benguiat-dead.html) published by the paper.

1558.title: Lotape, designed by Mustafa Eren, is on MyFonts!
1558.summary: Designed by Mustafa Eren, one of the prominent masters of contemporary calligraphy, and digitized by type designer Oğuzhan Cengiz, Lotape has been released on MyFonts. Drawing attention with its unusual ligature structure, Lotape stands out with its ornaments and rich alternates. Continuing his journey that began as a…
1558.content:
Designed by [Mustafa Eren](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100007154254756&comment_id=Y29tbWVudDoxMDE1ODc1NjkyODc4MzY4Nl8xMDE1ODc1NzIyOTcwMzY4Ng%3D%3D), one of the prominent masters of contemporary calligraphy, and digitized by type designer [Oğuzhan Cengiz](https://www.myfonts.com/foundry/hurufatfont-type-foundry/), [Lotape](https://www.myfonts.com/fonts/hurufatfont-type-foundry/lotape) has been released on MyFonts. Drawing attention with its unusual ligature structure, Lotape stands out with its ornaments and rich alternates.

Continuing his journey that began as a sign painter's apprentice in Denizli as the sole student of the lettering class at the Department of Graphic Design of the School of Applied Fine Arts in Istanbul, Mustafa Eren has developed more than sixty fonts since graduating in 1972, one of which was acquired by Letraset. Over the past decade, he has taken the art of calligraphy to a new level by interpreting it with Latin letters. Bringing together his original lettering works and font designs spanning nearly half a century in his book titled [Kaligrafik](https://www.idefix.com/Kitap/Kaligrafik/Sanat-Tasarim/Sanat-Tarihi-ve-Kurami/urunno=0001862545001), Mustafa Eren works as a lecturer at FSM Vakıf University.

1524.content:

1530.title: Cemal Akyıldız passed away at the age of 88.
1530.summary: The last master of the manual production era, and the final bridge between publishing illustrators and graphic designers, Cemal Akyıldız passed away at the age of 88 due to the pandemic. Born in Trabzon in 1932, Cemal Akyıldız moved to Istanbul in 1949 to study at the faculty of fine arts after graduating from…
1530.content:
The last master of the manual production era, and the final bridge between publishing illustrators and graphic designers, Cemal Akyıldız passed away at the age of 88 due to the pandemic.

Born in Trabzon in 1932, Cemal Akyıldız moved to Istanbul in 1949 to study at the faculty of fine arts after graduating from commercial high school. He studied under painters such as İbrahim Çallı and Hikmet Onat. Also apprenticing in painters’ studios during that period, Akyıldız interrupted his academic education to establish his own studio in Babıali at the age of 18. Continuing his work by producing book covers, movie posters, illustrations for school textbooks, and calligraphy, Akyıldız designed approximately two thousand novel covers. Having drawn portraits of all Turkish presidents starting with Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, Cemal Akyıldız worked as the official artist of Istanbul University for 25 years.

[Cemal Akyıldız](https://youtu.be/P5UYfMhUYps) was featured with his works in the *Cover Illustrators of Babıali* exhibition organized by Ömer Durmaz at Galeri Işık between May 23 and June 21, 2013, and gave an [interview](https://youtu.be/AadekPZCafU) in the sixth installment of the talks organized by GMK on December 21, 2019.

1471.title: Are typefaces political?
1471.summary: In his article, Hunter Schwarz examines the political connotations of typefaces through the study titled What’s in a Font?: Ideological Perceptions of Type, published in December 2019 in the journal Communications Studies by Virginia Tech professors Katherine Haenschen and Daniel J. Tamul. The study conducted with 987…
1471.content:
In his [article](https://yello.substack.com/p/do-fonts-have-a-political-party), Hunter Schwarz examines the political connotations of typefaces through the study titled [What’s in a Font?: Ideological Perceptions of Type](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10510974.2019.1692884?fbclid=IwAR3OSZisB0vhWnWLQimJY0LmJ0mv5UrT3f71h1QhY-aamzB9JPbyr4cxnes#.Xg9tFaHNYKQ.twitter), published in December 2019 in the journal *Communications Studies* by Virginia Tech professors Katherine Haenschen and Daniel J. Tamul. The study conducted with 987 participants reveals that typefaces carry ideological leanings, with serif and bold type conveying a conservative impression, while sans serif and italic type give a liberal one.

Lilly Smith’s [article](https://www.fastcompany.com/90458816/the-real-politics-of-type) published in [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com) regarding the same research.

1490.title: Sans Forgetica found not to improve memory.
1490.summary: Image/Video: Video Source In 2018, we shared the news of a font called Sans Forgetica, which was claimed to increase memory retention. Stephen Banham, a researcher who helped create Sans Forgetica, had stated that slanted letters with intermittent gaps acted as a simple puzzle for the reader; however, recent research…
1490.content:
*Image/Video: [Video Source](https://youtu.be/CEXzSehu5HM)*

In 2018, we [shared](https://wapo.st/2E4smGG) the news of a font called [Sans Forgetica](http://www.sansforgetica.rmit/), which was claimed to increase memory retention. Stephen Banham, a researcher who helped create Sans Forgetica, had stated that slanted letters with intermittent gaps acted as a simple puzzle for the reader; however, recent research revealed that this was not true. Following a study conducted on 400 students by psychology and design researchers from RMIT University, who designed the font, it was [announced](https://www.futurity.org/sans-forgetica-font-memory-2375842/) that Sans Forgetica does not improve memory.

Two typefaces, [Decimal](https://www.typography.com/fonts/decimal) and [Mercury](https://www.typography.com/fonts/mercury-text), by type foundry [Hoefler&Co](https://www.typography.com) led by [Jonathan Hoefler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Hoefler), [will be used](https://www.typography.com/blog/biden-fonts) in Joe Biden’s 2020 presidential campaign. The type foundry had previously designed [Gotham](https://www.typography.com/fonts/gotham/overview), used in Obama’s election campaign, and [Ringside](https://www.typography.com/fonts/ringside/overview), used in the visual identity of the Barack and Michelle Obama Foundation.

Following this development, [Steven Heller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Heller_(design_writer)) shared his thoughts in an article titled [Can Two Types Topple Trump?](https://www.printmag.com/post/the-daily-heller-can-two-types-topple-trump)

Additionally, [Decimal](https://www.typography.com/fonts/decimal/overview) was featured in the sixth episode of the second season of the Netflix documentary series [Abstract: The Art of Design](https://www.netflix.com/tr/title/80057883), starring Jonathan Hoefler as he researched antique watches for inspiration for a new typeface family. As the TTC, we also published an [article](https://medium.com/tipografi/soyut-düşünce-tasarım-sanatı-belgeseli-ve-bizim-büyük-terminoloji-çaresizliğimiz-77d7d844d4f4) addressing the terminology inconsistencies in the documentary.

1505.title: The letters of Sakarya are being brought to the digital realm.
1505.summary: Prepared as part of the master’s thesis by Ali Yıldırım, a student at the Sakarya University Institute of Social Sciences Department of Visual Communication Design, under the supervision of Asst. Prof. Dr. Murat Ertürk, the Letters of Sakarya project has been opened to digital access. Artifacts such as hand-painted…
1505.content:
Prepared as part of the master’s thesis by [Ali Yıldırım](https://www.behance.net/helloworldimali), a student at the Sakarya University Institute of Social Sciences [Department of Visual Communication Design](http://git.sakarya.edu.tr), under the supervision of Asst. Prof. Dr. [Murat Ertürk](http://muraterturk.com), the [Letters of Sakarya](http://sakaryaninharfleri.com) project has been opened to digital access. Artifacts such as hand-painted signs, plaques, apartment nameplates, window lettering, and graffiti on the streets of Sakarya dating back to the 1950s, along with findings related to the artisans who crafted them, are presented at [sakaryaninharfleri.com](http://sakaryaninharfleri.com).

Aiming to raise awareness of vernacular typography through graphic artifacts produced using traditional methods that are on the verge of disappearing, the findings obtained through the project not only contain data contributing locally to the city's visual communication and design history, but also constitute a visual archive that will be made available as open source for years to come.

Noting that versions…
1286.content:
Twitter [announced](https://twitter.com/TwitterDesign/status/1425505308563099650) that they have started using their new typeface, Chirp. Begun in January with the goal of designing a flexible, expressive, bold, agile, and fun typeface that reflects the voices making up Twitter, Chirp was developed in collaboration with the renowned type foundry [Grilli Type](https://www.grillitype.com). Noting that versions in Japanese, Chinese, and Arabic are also being developed in addition to Latin, Twitter’s Creative Director [Derrit DeRouen](https://www.derritderouen.com) [recounted](https://twitter.com/DerritDeRouen/status/1354548649561186306) the development process of the new typeface on his personal account. 🇬🇧

The change made by Twitter does not seem to have pleased the majority of users. So much so that 50% of users complained about the change, saying that the new typeface caused headaches and was less legible. Some users were even bewildered by a change that could lead to confusing the *Follow* and *Unfollow* buttons. Following Aaron Mak’s [interview](https://slate.com/technology/2021/08/twitter-font-redesign-chirp-franklin-gothic.html) with 8chan founder Fredrick Brennan to better understand what was going on, Daniel Piper also [addressed](https://www.creativebloq.com/amp/news/new-twitter-font?mc_cid=c09e6e0c9e&mc_eid=48a95a3cf1) user dissatisfaction. 🇬🇧

1287.content:

Type designer [Marie Boulanger](http://marie-boulanger.com) has written a book titled [*XX, XY: Sex, Letters and Stereotypes*](https://www.dezeen.com/2021/08/05/xx-xy-book-marie-boulanger-gender-typography/) about how we make gender-based judgments through letterforms—a hotly debated topic in France—and how this perpetuates various gender stereotypes. 1288.title: The mystery of the lowercase letter g
1288.summary: Image/Video: Video Source “We think if we look at something, especially if we have to pay attention to its shape as in reading, we know what it looks like, but the results show that is not always the case.” Michael McCloskey Johns Hopkins researchers conducted a three-part experiment to test people’s awareness of the…
1288.content:
*Image/Video: [Video Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iSNGaJ0KiEs)*

> “We think if we look at something, especially if we have to pay attention to its shape as in reading, we know what it looks like, but the results show that is not always the case.” [Michael McCloskey](http://cogsci.jhu.edu/directory/michael-mccloskey/)

Johns Hopkins researchers conducted a [three-part experiment](https://hub.jhu.edu/2018/04/03/two-versions-of-letter-g-brain-science/) to test people’s awareness of the *g* they tend to write versus the *g* they tend to read. The experiment revealed that despite seeing it millions of times in almost every book, novel, newspaper, and email, people are actually unaware of the more common form of the lowercase letter *g*. 🇬🇧

Located in the city of Dresden, East Germany’s only type foundry, Typoart, was established through the nationalization of type foundries such as *Schelter & Giesecke*, *Schriftguss*, and *Ludwig Wagner*. The type foundry’s art direction was held by [Herbert Thannhäuser](http://luc.devroye.org/fonts-24777.html) until 1963 and by [Albert Kapr](https://www.linotype.com/fr/7311/albert-kapr.html) until 1987.

1357.title: Is stretching type always wrong?
1357.summary: Everyone who studies typography knows that stretching type horizontally or vertically is wrong, because stretching type distorts the anatomy of glyphs meticulously defined by type designers and disrupts the carefully arranged harmony of typesetting. However, type designer Roman Gornitsky says that in some cases,…
1357.content:
Everyone who studies typography knows that stretching type horizontally or vertically is wrong, because stretching type distorts the anatomy of glyphs meticulously defined by type designers and disrupts the carefully arranged harmony of typesetting. However, type designer [Roman Gornitsky](https://www.myfonts.com/person/Roman_Gornitsky/) [says](https://letters.temporarystate.net/entry/6/) that in some cases, breaking the delicately tuned harmony of proportional typesetting is precisely what one should look for. 🇬🇧 Gornitsky’s proposition recalls Robin Rendle’s sentence: “[challenging what we know about typography is the first step to contributing to its future.](https://medium.com/tipografi/tipografinin-gelece%C4%9Fi-8c4b01c088b3)”

[READING RECOMMENDATION: “The Future of Typography” — *Robin Rendle, January 6, 2017*](https://medium.com/tipografi/tipografinin-gelece%C4%9Fi-8c4b01c088b3)

1372.title: A variable font drawing attention to the climate crisis: “Climate Crisis”
1372.summary: The variable font Climate Crisis was commissioned by the Nordic region’s largest newspaper, Helsingin Sanomat, to help people see the urgency of climate change more concretely. Available as a free download, the font is based on Arctic sea ice data from the National Snow and Ice Data Center between 1979 and 2019, as…
1372.content:
The variable font [Climate Crisis](https://kampanjat.hs.fi/climatefont/) was commissioned by the Nordic region’s largest newspaper, [Helsingin Sanomat](https://www.hs.fi), to help people see the urgency of climate change more concretely. Available as a free download, the font is based on Arctic sea ice data from the [National Snow and Ice Data Center](https://nsidc.org) between 1979 and 2019, as well as forecasts up to 2050 from the [Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change](https://www.ipcc.ch/srocc/). Featuring OpenType capabilities, this variable font offers a collection of weights ranging from bold to light representing the years 1979, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2019, 2030, 2040, and 2050. In this way, as the years go by, the impact of climate change can be observed through the variable font.

Monotype [announced](https://www.monotype.com/company/news/monotype-announces-acquisition-iconic-type-foundry-hoeflerco) that it has acquired the renowned type foundry [Hoefler&Co](https://www.typography.com), founded in 1989 by Jonathan Hoefler. 1308.content:
The [TypoArabic](https://twitter.com/typo_arabic) project [announced](https://research.reading.ac.uk/typoarabic/taking-stock-and-looking-ahead/) that they will be publishing a new book on Arabic typography in the coming months. Authored by [Titus Nemeth](https://twitter.com/tntype), the book—currently in draft form—will include contributions from Emanuela Conidi, Borna Izadpanah, and Gerry Leonidas, as well as [Onur Yazıcıgil](http://www.onuryazicigil.com) from our country. The book will consist of two parts: scholarly articles on historical aspects of Arabic typography and practical design considerations for current practitioners.

[TypoArabic](https://research.reading.ac.uk/typoarabic/introducing-typoarabic/) is a three-year research project funded by the European Commission under the [Horizon 2020](https://ec.europa.eu/research/mariecurieactions/msca-actions_en) program at the [Department of Typography & Graphic Communication at the University of Reading](http://www.reading.ac.uk/typography/typ-homepage.aspx).

1320.content:
*Image/Video: [Video Source](https://youtu.be/RmIVEnrhURI)*

A [short documentary](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RmIVEnrhURI) produced about Dutch typographer Thomas Gravemaker. Having started printing in 1970, Thomas Gravemaker worked for many years with various publishers in the UK—including several years as a senior designer at Thames & Hudson—and as a studio manager in a design group in France before founding his own workshop. His passion for letterpress began before his studies at the [Gerrit Rietveld Academie](https://rietveldacademie.nl) in Amsterdam and developed over the years. During these years, he worked on private commissions, taught letterpress, and lectured at various conferences and events.

1321.title: ILT launches its font store for users.
1321.summary: The typography blog I Love Typography (ILT), founded by John Boardley, introduced its new ecosystem combining font discovery and licensing with an innovative e-commerce platform. Launching a store with 7,000 fonts from 40 type foundries, ILT also makes it possible to search for fonts based on formal qualities—from…
1321.content:
The typography blog [I Love Typography (ILT)](https://fonts.ilovetypography.com), founded by [John Boardley](https://twitter.com/johnboardley), introduced its new ecosystem combining font discovery and licensing with an innovative e-commerce platform. Launching a store with 7,000 fonts from 40 type foundries, ILT also makes it possible to search for fonts based on formal qualities—from general characteristics like contrast, rhythm, energy, axis, and structure down to details like serif shapes—using its font description system called [CEDARS+](https://fonts.ilovetypography.com/cedars).

Following Monotype’s major move toward monopolization by acquiring FontShop in 2014, new and alternative sales channels such as [Fontstand](https://fontstand.com), [Future Fonts](https://www.futurefonts.xyz), and [Type Network](https://www.typenetwork.com) had emerged. This move by ILT also stands as one of the most significant developments in recent times. On the other hand, [criticism](https://twitter.com/amsterdam_type/status/1409607042168410118) has begun to emerge over whether a blog that writes about fonts—even if not considered reviews or critiques—selling fonts would create a conflict of interest.

Readers who wish to do further reading can check out the in-depth article on [CEDARS+](https://fonts.ilovetypography.com/cedars), developed in collaboration with [Nadine Chahine](https://twitter.com/arabictype), [here](https://ilovetypography.com/2021/06/28/talking-about-type-introducing-cedars/), and Steven Heller’s interview with Nadine Chahine [here](https://www.printmag.com/post/the-daily-heller-i-love-you-love-we-love-typography). 🇬🇧

Coordinated by [Prof. Fiona Ross](https://www.reading.ac.uk/typography/staff/professor-fiona-ross) and conducted by [Dr. Alice Savoie](https://twitter.com/alicesavoie) and Dr. Helena Lekka, the website for the [Women in Type](https://www.women-in-type.com) research project has launched. 1334.title: Ali Saraç, brush sign painter of Ordu
1334.summary: Researcher Güven Bayar has brought to light the work of Ali Saraç, who worked as a brush sign painter in Ordu during the 1960s. Born in Trabzon in 1926, Ali Saraç went to Istanbul in the late 1940s and learned gold leaf and rubber stamp techniques from Armenian masters in Karaköy. After returning to Trabzon to open…
1334.content:
Researcher [Güven Bayar](https://twitter.com/guvenbayar_) has [brought to light](http://www.haberaltas.com/tr-TR/haberler/8232/caginin-otesinde-bir-sanatkar-ali-sarac) the work of Ali Saraç, who worked as a brush sign painter in Ordu during the 1960s. Born in Trabzon in 1926, Ali Saraç went to Istanbul in the late 1940s and learned gold leaf and rubber stamp techniques from Armenian masters in Karaköy. After returning to Trabzon to open his first shop and work as a sign painter, Ali Saraç—whose signs were used across a wide region from the Black Sea to Eastern Anatolia—passed away in 1980.

1419.content:
Following Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan has also decided to switch to the Latin alphabet. [According to the report covered in Prof. Dr. Kürşad Zorlu’s column](https://www.haberturk.com/yazarlar/prof-dr-kursad-zorlu/2988416-kazakistandan-sonra-ozbekistan-da-latin-alfabesi-karari-aldi), starting January 1, 2023, all activities and official correspondence of institutions and organizations in the country will be conducted in the Latin alphabet. 1422.title: Proxima Vara: The variable version of Proxima Nova
1422.summary: Proxima Vara, the variable version of Mark Simonson’s famous typeface Proxima Nova, has been released. The famous type family, which Simonson began sketching in the early 1980s and emerged under the name Visigothic in the early 1990s, was announced to the public in 1994 under the name Proxima Sans. In 2002, the rising…
1422.content:
[Proxima Vara](https://proxima-vara.marksimonson.com), the variable version of [Mark Simonson](https://www.marksimonson.com)’s famous typeface [Proxima Nova](https://www.marksimonson.com/fonts/view/proxima-nova), has been released. The famous type family, which Simonson began sketching in the early 1980s and emerged under the name *Visigothic* in the early 1990s, was announced to the public in 1994 under the name Proxima Sans. In 2002, the rising popularity of Gotham created a new demand for geometric typefaces, paving the way for Proxima Sans. That same year, Rolling Stone magazine began using Proxima Sans as part of its redesign led by Matthew Ball. Proxima Nova, the revised version of Proxima Sans, was commercially released for the first time in 2005.

1260.content:

The selected typeface will begin being used in 2022.

1272.content:

1221.title: An article on legibility from Ralf Herrmann
1221.summary: “Word shape is no longer a viable model of word recognition. 1221.content:
> “Word shape is no longer a viable model of word recognition. The majority of scientific evidence shows that we recognise the letters that make up the word and then use this visual information to recognise the word.”

> Kevin Larson

[Ralf Herrmann](https://twitter.com/opentype) has written [an article](https://typography.guru/journal/how-do-we-read-words-and-how-should-we-set-them-r19/) addressing important information on the concept of legibility, discussing how science has overturned conventional ideas that we perceive words as a whole and how ascenders and descenders in typographic anatomy support efficient reading. Herrmann’s article is significant in reminding us that, especially regarding legibility and readability, rather than relying on memorized assumptions without considering ambient environments and conditions, one must consult the findings of scientific research conducted in this field! 🇬🇧

Pointing out that in an era where there are more educational opportunities and more type is designed than at any time in history, it is surprising to encounter less discussion about type than ever, the platform is spearheaded by [Peter Biľak](https://peterbilak.com) and [Andrej Krátky](https://www.typotheque.com/authors/andrej_kratky) and edited by type and design historian [Dan Reynolds](https://www.typeoff.de/about-dan-reynolds/), known from [TypeOff](https://www.typeoff.de), who focuses on late 19th-century type foundries.

The [first book review](https://fontstand.com/news/book-reviews/a-grammar-of-typography/) on Fontstand News is Mark Argetsinger’s book [A Grammar of Typography: Classical Book Design in the Digital Age](https://www.amazon.com/Grammar-Typography-Classical-Design-Digital/dp/1567926533).

1226.title: Helvetica Now Variable
1226.summary: Monotype announced the variable version of Helvetica Now via its Twitter account. With the goal of creating a Helvetica that meets the needs of today's designers and creatives, the update process—involving dozens of designers and engineers—began in December 2014, and following five years of work, Helvetica Now was…
1226.content:
Monotype announced the variable version of Helvetica Now [via its Twitter account](https://twitter.com/Monotype/status/1413656250840227843). With the goal of creating a Helvetica that meets the needs of today's designers and creatives, the update process—involving dozens of designers and engineers—began in December 2014, and following five years of work, [Helvetica Now](https://www.monotype.com/fonts/helvetica-now) was released in 2019. Offering over one million weights in a single font file and over two and a half million in the italic version, the new [Helvetica Now Variable](https://www.monotype.com/fonts/helvetica-now-variable) delivers customized options across the weight, optical size, and width axes.

Born in 1941 in the Salem Valley of Germany, near the Swiss border, Weingart defied the traditional rules of the…
1229.content:
Following Reynold Ruffins, another sad piece of news came from Switzerland. Internationally renowned graphic designer and typographer [Wolfgang Weingart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfgang_Weingart) passed away on July 12, 2021, in Basel, Switzerland. Born in 1941 in the Salem Valley of Germany, near the Swiss border, Weingart defied the traditional rules of the Swiss Style in typography, pioneering the *New Wave* or *Swiss Punk* styles.

1230.summary: Cardiff and Amsterdam-based design studio Smörgåsbord is designing a typeface that allows the unique characteristics of the Welsh language to be expressed. Developed in collaboration with Colophon Type Foundry, the typeface named Cymru Wales includes the eight digraphs that distinguish the Welsh alphabet from the…
1230.content:
Cardiff and Amsterdam-based design studio [Smörgåsbord](https://www.smorgasbordstudio.com/) is designing a typeface that allows the unique characteristics of the Welsh language to be expressed. Developed in collaboration with [Colophon Type Foundry](https://www.colophon-foundry.org/), the typeface named *Cymru Wales* includes the eight digraphs that distinguish the Welsh alphabet from the English alphabet. The project was commissioned by the Welsh government as part of the nation's rebranding.

165.title: Typography, Automation, and the Division of Labor
165.summary: “Typography was born with the mass-production mechanism of the printing press; thus, through its perpetual relationship with automation, it has taken part in the distinctly modern dynamics of overwork, underemployment, and runaway production.” J. Dakota Brown’s booklet titled “Typography, Automation, and the Division…
165.content:
> “Typography was born with the mass-production mechanism of the printing press; thus, through its perpetual relationship with automation, it has taken part in the distinctly modern dynamics of overwork, underemployment, and runaway production.”

[J. Dakota Brown](https://linktr.ee/jdakota)’s booklet titled “[Typography, Automation, and the Division of Labor](https://otherforms.net/typography-automation-and-the-division-of-labor/)”, published in a limited run in 2019 by [Other Forms Books](https://otherforms.net), in which he reinterprets the history of graphic design by linking it to the history of capitalism, is now available online. Brown, who studied graphic design at North Carolina State University and critical theory at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, had published a booklet titled “[The Power of Design as a Dream of Autonomy](https://i-n-g-a.com/products/the-power-of-design-as-a-dream-of-autonomy)” in the same year; Ksenya Samarskaya from the *AIGA Eye on Design* team also conducted an [interview](https://eyeondesign.aiga.org/designer-educator-j-dakota-brown-is-untangling-the-relationship-between-design-and-labor/) with Brown in 2021. 🇬🇧

167.title: New typography book: “The Typographic Medium”
167.summary: New York University faculty member Kate Brideau, in her book titled “The Typographic Medium” published by The MIT Press in 2021, presents an innovative examination of typography as a medium of communication rather than merely a component of print or digital media. Examining the tension between the often-overlooked…
167.content:
New York University faculty member [Kate Brideau](https://www.stern.nyu.edu/faculty/bio/kate-brideau), in her book titled “[The Typographic Medium](https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262045858/)” published by [The MIT Press](https://mitpress.mit.edu/) in 2021, presents an innovative examination of typography as a medium of communication rather than merely a component of print or digital media. Examining the tension between the often-overlooked *typographic form* and the frequently dominant *function*, Brideau argues that typography consists of shapes rather than letters, and that these shapes are existentially and technologically at the heart of the typographic medium. 🇬🇧

173.title: Monotype acquires Berthold’s renowned typefaces.
173.summary: Akzidenz-Grotesk, one of the world’s first widely used sans-serif typefaces that inspired many subsequent type designs including Helvetica, joins the Monotype family along with more than 700 historic typefaces from the Berthold library. 🇬🇧 The inventory and digital typeface distribution rights of the Berthold Type…
173.content:
Akzidenz-Grotesk, one of the world’s first widely used sans-serif typefaces that inspired many subsequent type designs including Helvetica, [joins](https://www.monotype.com/company/news/monotype-acquires-bertholds-renowned-typeface-inventory) the Monotype family along with more than 700 historic typefaces from the Berthold library. 🇬🇧 The inventory and digital typeface distribution rights of the [Berthold Type Foundry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berthold_Type_Foundry), founded in Berlin by Hermann Berthold in 1858, were acquired in 1997 by [Berthold Types Limited](https://www.bertholdtypes.com). Alongside Akzidenz-Grotesk, this inventory also includes beloved typefaces such as Imago, Cosmos, Formata, Block, Solemnis, and City.

As the studio’s first publication, the book offers a detailed examination of two type…
92.content:
Designed by [MuirMcNeil](https://muirmcneil.com/), the book [System Process Form](https://vol.co/product/system-process-form/), showcasing hundreds of visual examples drawn from the studio’s two type systems and printed throughout in three neon inks and metallic black, was published by Unit Editions. As the studio’s first publication, the book offers a detailed examination of two type systems—an extensive collection of geometric alphabets where every line, shape, letterform, and word is designed to collaborate. In [their interview with Steven Heller](https://www.printmag.com/daily-heller/the-daily-heller-a-newer-new-typography/), McNeil says that this book is "a potent testament to the beauty of analytical approaches to form-making for visual communication, a book that embraces both micro and macro viewpoints and can be as magnificent as its results." 🇬🇧

32.title: New book on Arabic typography
32.summary: An outcome of the TypoArabic Research Project announced last year and concluded on June 3, 2022, the book titled “Arabic Typography History and Practice” has been published by Niggli Verlag. Led by Titus Nemeth with a foreword by Robert Bringhurst, and featuring contributions from figures such as Emanuela Conidi,…
32.content:
An outcome of the *TypoArabic* Research Project announced last year and concluded on June 3, 2022, the book titled “[Arabic Typography History and Practice](https://www.niggli.ch/en/produkt/arabic-typography/)” has been published by [Niggli Verlag](https://www.niggli.ch/en/). Led by Titus Nemeth with a foreword by Robert Bringhurst, and featuring contributions from figures such as Emanuela Conidi, Borna Izadpanah, Gerry Leonidas, and Onur Yazıcıgil from Turkey, this 416-page book offers comprehensive content on Arabic typography. The first section brings together a group of young scholars researching the subject, providing an in-depth synthesis of the typographic history and development of Arabic script. In the second section, these historical foundations are complemented by a concise guide to Arabic typography through the lens of a designer. Bonus: [Titus Nemeth’s article on the book](https://research.reading.ac.uk/typoarabic/arabic-typography-history-and-practice-is-out-now/) ➚

Oliver Schöndorfer published his conversation with Nadine Chahine on Arabic typography and type design in two parts on his [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/c/PimpmyType). In the [first part](https://youtu.be/rwIbkOs2LkI) of the conversation, Chahine explores why the Arabic script was neglected for so long and shares the state of Arabic type design in the late 1990s. 121.title: Berlin’s typographic heritage is being digitized.
121.summary: Four institutions from Berlin have collaborated to digitize a large portion of their collections of printed type specimens and make them accessible online for free. Stiftung Deutsches Technikmuseum Berlin, Erik Spiekermann Foundation gGmbH, Kunstbibliothek der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin, and Staatsbibliothek zu…
121.content:
Four institutions from Berlin [have collaborated](https://fontstand.com/news/design-news/berlins-typographic-legacy/) to digitize a large portion of their collections of printed type specimens and make them accessible online for free. *Stiftung Deutsches Technikmuseum Berlin*, *Erik Spiekermann Foundation gGmbH*, *Kunstbibliothek der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin*, and *Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin* applied for funding for a joint project. The funding was granted by the Funding Program for the Digitization of Cultural Assets of the State of Berlin (digiS). 136.title: Nebiolo’s typefaces

136.content:
As part of the [Nebiolo History Project](http://nebiolohistory.org), Riccardo Olocco published [an article](https://fontstand.com/news/essays/typefaces-in-search-of-an-author/) featuring an analysis of the archival materials that survived after the closure of Nebiolo, one of Italy’s most famous type foundries. 🇬🇧 The resulting data aims to define the role played by the type design office known as the *Studio Artistico* in creating the Nebiolo typefaces it produced. Until its closure in 1978, the Turin-based Nebiolo company was Italy's major type foundry both nationally and internationally for most of the twentieth century. Founded in 1852, Nebiolo successfully expanded as an important printing press manufacturer. It dominated the Italian market in the production of printing machinery and foundry type until the end of letterpress printing in the 1970s.

138.content:
When Indonesia gained independence in 1945, the Latin alphabet was made mandatory for the country's administrative affairs, and the everyday use of the Javanese script effectively ceased. Although the Javanese script is still taught as a mandatory subject in schools across various parts of [Java](https://tr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cava), most people feel alienated from the language and view it as a static relic rather than a living alphabet. In his [article](https://typegeist.org/article/rediscovering-design-in-a-supplanted-script-the-case-of-javanese), Aditya Bayu Perdana discusses the turbulent history of the Javanese script and its relationship with contemporary design. 🇬🇧

For the first time, the 2022 prize was awarded to two individuals. [Prof. Dr. Jeffrey F. Hamburger](https://haa.fas.harvard.edu/people/jeffrey-f-hamburger), an expert in late medieval book illustration and the transition to the era of the printing press, shared the prize with printing professor [Eckehart Schumacher-Gebler](https://www.hbksaar.de/personen/details/schumachergebler). 153.title: The type designs of Rudolf Koch
153.summary: Image/Video: Video Source A presentation by Dr. Dorothee Ader, director of the Klingspor Museum, on the type designs, letterings, and drawings of German type designer, calligrapher, and illustrator Rudolf Koch (1876–1934). 🇬🇧 Having spent his youth working as an apprentice in a metal workshop in Hanau, Koch later…
153.content:
*Image/Video: [Video Source](https://youtu.be/HCpMYO_Sgrg)*

A [presentation](https://youtu.be/HCpMYO_Sgrg) by Dr. Dorothee Ader, director of the [Klingspor Museum](https://www.klingspor-museum.de), on the type designs, letterings, and drawings of German type designer, calligrapher, and illustrator [Rudolf Koch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolf_Koch) (1876–1934). 🇬🇧 Having spent his youth working as an apprentice in a metal workshop in Hanau, Koch later began studying at the Nuremberg Academy of Fine Arts. Between 1897 and 1906, he worked at various businesses related to bookselling in Leipzig. He designed book covers in the Art Nouveau style, the popular movement of the time. In 1906, he began working at the Rudhard Foundry in Offenbach—which later became the Klingspor Type Foundry—where prominent designers such as Otto Eckmann and Peter Behrens worked. Known for typefaces such as [Neuland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuland) and [Kabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabel_(typeface)) created for the Klingspor Type Foundry, Koch passed away from a heart attack in 1934 at the age of just 57.

44.title: An exhibition held in memory of Ange Degheest
44.summary: Type design workshop students from EESAB, an art academy in the Brittany region of France, along with their instructors, organized an exhibition in memory of French type designer Ange Degheest (1928–2009) as part of the Une saison graphique 2020 festival. The exhibition features original objects and documents from…
44.content:
Type design workshop students from [EESAB](https://www.eesab.fr), an art academy in the Brittany region of France, along with their instructors, organized an [exhibition](https://velvetyne.fr/degheest/infos.html) in memory of French type designer Ange Degheest (1928–2009) as part of the *Une saison graphique 2020* festival. The [exhibition](https://velvetyne.fr/degheest/infos.html) features original objects and documents from personal archives opened to the public for the first time concerning the designer, who has been largely forgotten and bore witness to the technical upheavals in printing and telecommunications during the second half of the twentieth century. In addition, as part of the exhibition, Poem Editions published a twenty-four-page [booklet](https://www.poem-editions.com/products/degheest) that includes an essay titled “The female ghost of French type history” by [Alice Savoie](https://twitter.com/alicesavoie?utm_source=aposto), whose project [Women in Type](https://www.women-in-type.com/) we covered extensively in January’s [Typography Bulletin](https://apos.to/s/61bf2de91486a5000641a573). Degheest’s type designs were revived and made available under an open font license through the [Velvetyne Type Foundry](http://velvetyne.fr/fonts/degheest/) website. 🇬🇧

191.content:
The book about Boğos Tatikyan, a painter and printer from Izmir, prepared by our founding member [Ömer Durmaz](https://twitter.com/omerdurmaz) and İskender Dereli, has been published by the Izmir Development Agency. Boğos Tatikyan, a painter and printer from Izmir, depicted Ottoman sultans, ordinary people he observed in and around the city of Izmir, and particularly intriguing figures from different communities, reproducing them using the lithography (stone printing) technique in his own printing house and offering them for sale. The lithographs, printed in single color on single sheets, were hand-colored with watercolors using a brush, and printed in portable and storable sizes. The book on Tatikyan, who played an important role in providing access to colorful visual sources regarding the folklore and history of Ottoman Izmir, can be read online [here](https://kulturyayinlari.izka.org.tr/tatikyann).

209.content:
[Astrid Stavro](https://twitter.com/AstridStavro) [has become](https://www.instagram.com/p/CZPSigDMoE2/) the new president of the International Society of Typographic Designers ([ISTD](https://www.istd.org.uk)). After studying philosophy and literature at Boston University, Stavro completed her graphic design education at Central Saint Martins. She later attended the Royal College of Art. There, she met Jeff Willis, who influenced her education and gave her a humble perspective on life and graphic design. Co-founder of Design by Atlas, Stavro was elected a member of the Alliance Graphique Internationale (AGI) in 2010. Between 2018 and 2021, she was a partner at Pentagram. Stavro is cited as an exemplar of the idea of adopting an outward-looking global perspective within the discipline.

177.title: A faster reading experience with Bionic Reading
177.summary: Developed by Swiss designer Renato Casutt as a result of six years of research, Bionic Reading claims to provide faster reading by guiding the brain to complete the rest of the word when its initial letters are highlighted. The project, which began development in 2016, was supported by the Swiss InnoSuisse Institute,…
177.content:
Developed by Swiss designer [Renato Casutt](https://twitter.com/renato_casutt) as a result of six years of research, [Bionic Reading](https://bionic-reading.com/) claims to provide faster reading by guiding the brain to complete the rest of the word when its initial letters are highlighted. The project, which began development in 2016, was supported by the Swiss InnoSuisse Institute, and it was announced that a small preliminary study would be conducted with a Swiss university in the coming months. However, criticism of this claim was not long in coming. Prof. Lauren M. Singer Trakhman from the University of Maryland [wrote](https://theconversation.com/can-bionic-reading-make-you-a-speed-reader-not-so-fast-183905) that the sample size of 12 was too small, that it had not been tested on people with dyslexia, and that the claim was overstated since it had not been subjected to standard scientific testing. Ralf Hermann published a critical [video](https://youtu.be/V53tbzy9n9w) on his YouTube channel. Meanwhile, the Readwise team conducted a quick experiment to test whether Bionic Reading actually works, and early results [show](https://blog.readwise.io/does-bionic-reading-actually-work/) that the speed-reading claim is not entirely accurate. 🇬🇧

842.title: Modern handwriting: A historical survey
842.summary: In the bulletin we published in August—or haven’t you subscribed yet? :)—we mentioned TypeTogether’s comprehensive research on handwriting models taught in Western schools and their resulting project called Primarium. It appears that Typotheque is also conducting its own research. As part of this research, French…
842.content:
[In the bulletin we published in August](https://medium.com/tipografi/tipografi-b%C3%BClteni-a%C4%9Fustos-2023-5ee8b04702ec)—or haven’t you subscribed yet? :)—we mentioned TypeTogether’s comprehensive research on handwriting models taught in Western schools and their resulting project called [Primarium](https://primarium.info/). It appears that Typotheque is also conducting its own research. As part of this research, French researcher and author Sébastien Morlighem published a five-part [article series](https://www.typotheque.com/articles/modern-handwriting-a-historical-survey-1) on handwriting. 🇬🇧 In the series, Morlighem presents a historical survey of modern handwriting through articles covering new approaches in Great Britain, models from America and Western Europe, handwriting in Cyrillic and Greek scripts, and cursive italic handwriting in Central Europe. All this research was certainly not in vain! After researching educational handwriting models for over a year and documenting the evolution of handwriting in the Western world, the Typotheque team developed a typeface called [Dash](https://www.typotheque.com/blog/dash-a-typeface-with-different-speeds-and-expressions), which not only utilizes the collective characteristics of handwriting as taught in schools, but also mimics how handwriting transforms over time into an individual’s personal expression.

850.content:
The first version of [Invert](https://www.futurefonts.xyz/anna-khorash/invert), described by [Anna Khorash](https://www.instagram.com/horashann/) as “an experimental variable typeface with interpolation between shapes and counter-shapes,” has been released on Future Fonts. While the styles can work separately, the magic happens in the movement between them.

806.title: Sungu Çapan passed away at the age of 76.
806.summary: “In 1960s Turkey, Yeni Sinema magazine was virtually the Ray Gun of the 1990s that we know so well from the history of world design! And graphic designer Sungu Çapan, of course, was the David Carson of that era!” — Ömer Durmaz Film writer and critic Sungu Çapan passed away at the age of 76. Better known for his film…
806.content:
> “In 1960s Turkey, Yeni Sinema magazine was virtually the Ray Gun of the 1990s that we know so well from the history of world design! And graphic designer Sungu Çapan, of course, was the David Carson of that era!” — Ömer Durmaz

Film writer and critic Sungu Çapan passed away at the age of 76. Better known for his film writing, while also an accomplished graphic designer who graduated from the State Academy of Fine Arts Department of Graphic Arts, Çapan was among the first figures in our country to grasp contemporary typography, and the covers of *Yeni Sinema* magazine, a publication of the Turkish Cinematheque Association, are of great significance to our design history.

918.title: Monotype continues to monopolize.

918.content:
In our past bulletins, we drew attention to Monotype’s monopolization in the type industry by covering its acquisitions. Following Monotype’s acquisition of Berthold’s typefaces and renowned type foundries such as Fontsmith, URW, and Hoefler&Co, a comprehensive [article](https://qz.com/2068310/what-monotypes-purchase-of-hoeflerco-means-to-font-designers/) was published on the monopolization of the type industry; Nuclear Bits [evaluated](https://nuclearbits.com/bye-hoefler-monotype-hello-commissioner/) the impact of the Hoefler&Co acquisition on their company. Typographica also voiced its reaction by making a [post](https://twitter.com/typographica/status/1563262628322873347/photo/1) stating that most users have no idea that the vast majority of the type industry is controlled by a single company. Most recently, Monotype [announced](https://www.monotype.com/company/press-release/fontworks-plans-to-join-monotype) that it has agreed to acquire [Fontworks](https://en.fontworks.co.jp/), the iconic Tokyo-based type foundry that has contributed to shaping type culture in Japan over the last thirty years. Notable as Monotype’s first acquisition in Japan, the deal is slated to close in the third quarter of 2023. 🇬🇧

921.title: Twitter’s logo has changed!
921.summary: Elon Musk announced Twitter’s new logo. Even though experts warned that rebranding could be a risky move, the new logo began to be used. Musk had attempted to rebrand PayPal under the same name in 2000, but was ousted by the board of directors. Musk’s choice of a Unicode character numbered U+1D54F, designed for use by…
921.content:
Elon Musk [announced](https://twitter.com/elonmusk/status/1683877911315599360?s=20) Twitter’s new logo. Even though experts [warned](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2023/jul/24/elon-musk-reveals-the-new-twitter-logo-x) that rebranding could be a risky move, the new logo began to be used. Musk had attempted to rebrand PayPal under the same name in 2000, but was [ousted](https://www.disconnect.blog/p/elon-musk-wants-to-relive-his-start) by the board of directors. Musk’s choice of a Unicode character numbered [U+1D54F](https://www.compart.com/en/unicode/U+1D54F), designed for use by mathematicians, as the new logo was widely debated. Although the new logo was [compared](https://twitter.com/willphoto/status/1684036856646868992) to the character X in Monotype’s typeface *Special Alphabet 4*, it was [clarified](https://twitter.com/monotype/status/1683836498175750144) that Monotype’s creative director Phil Garnham examined the logo and that there is no similarity to the character in the aforementioned typeface. Louis Ashworth from the Financial Times wrote a detailed [article](https://www.ft.com/content/da262b2a-f39a-466b-9b2f-2f8fa84f0117) on the matter. Gerry Leonidas, on the other hand, shared his thoughts via his [LinkedIn account](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/gerryleonidas_yesterday-i-got-asked-by-a-journalist-a-few-activity-7089627589744435200-JC_q/). According to him, based on absolute criteria, the new logo is a bad design—especially for digital environments—and conceptually weak. 🇬🇧

924.title: Albert Boton has passed away.
924.summary: French type designer Albert Boton (1932–2023) has passed away. 🇬🇧 In 1952, while apprenticing alongside his carpenter father, Boton discovered graphic design when he visited the advertising agency Atelier Troy in Paris to replace its window. He enrolled at École Estienne, where he took classes from Adrian Frutiger.…
924.content:
French type designer Albert Boton (1932–2023) has [passed away](https://fontstand.com/news/design-news/albert-boton-19322023/). 🇬🇧 In 1952, while apprenticing alongside his carpenter father, Boton discovered graphic design when he visited the advertising agency Atelier Troy in Paris to replace its window. He enrolled at École Estienne, where he took classes from Adrian Frutiger. Following his education, he joined the Deberny & Peignot Type Foundry, where he had the opportunity to work alongside figures such as Adrian Frutiger, Ladislas Mandel, and Lucette Girard. Achieving international success with Eras in 1961, Boton worked for Paris's largest advertising agencies and created numerous type designs such as Elan, Carrénoir, Scherzo, Pompei, and Linex Sans.

619.title: A new book from Richard Ardagh: “Type Archived”
619.summary: Founded in London in 1992, the Type Archive amassed nearly eight million items over the years, but closed in 2023. Highlights of the archive included antique materials from Stephenson Blake, the type foundry active in Britain from the early nineteenth century until the 1990s; hot-metal technology from The Monotype…
619.content:
Founded in London in 1992, the *Type Archive* amassed nearly eight million items over the years, but closed in 2023. Highlights of the archive included antique materials from Stephenson Blake, the type foundry active in Britain from the early nineteenth century until the 1990s; hot-metal technology from The Monotype Corporation; and innovative wood type produced at Robert DeLittle’s factory. Type Archive volunteer Richard Ardagh’s book “[Type Archived: A visual journey through typographic history](https://vol.co/collections/type-archived)” sheds light on materials significant to both the history of art and engineering. **☞ Recommended Reading: **Steven Heller’s [interview](https://www.printmag.com/daily-heller/the-daily-heller-saving-the-printing-historys-precious-metals-and-wood/) with Ardagh about the fate of the archive and the new book.

708.title: ISType at Salt Galata on November 2–3!
708.summary: Held for the ninth time this year, the ISType conference will take place at Salt Galata between November 2–3, 2024, with the theme “Text-ure”. As the conference's first speaker, Tobias Frere-Jones will trace his journey from high school student to professional designer and the insights gained along the way through his…
708.content:
Held for the ninth time this year, the [ISType conference](https://istype.com/2024/) will take place at Salt Galata between November 2–3, 2024, with the theme “Text-ure”.

As the conference's first speaker, [Tobias Frere-Jones](https://frerejones.com/) will trace his journey from high school student to professional designer and the insights gained along the way through his projects. Following Frere-Jones, [Ulrike Rausch](https://liebefonts.com/), known for her script typefaces, will demonstrate how she combines countless ligatures and alternate letterforms with modern font technologies and how she creates script typefaces. Marc Schütz, creative director of [Studio Schultzschultz](https://schultzschultz.com/), which specializes in corporate design and branding, will explore the design processes of custom type design projects combining typography and creative coding; Astrid Stavro will discuss her experience of growing up surrounded by ink and paper in a print shop and how this led to her fascination with letters and language; and [Eben Sorkin](https://www.sorkintype.com/) will share in-depth insights into the issue of optical size in typefaces. In the afternoon program, [Bartu Başaran](https://atelierbartubasaran.com/) will present on a Greek typeface revived from the monumental inscriptions of Perge, while [Albert-Jan Pool](https://www.instagram.com/albertjanpool/) will give a presentation on serendipity in type design, drawing from his encounter with the DIN 1451 typeface. [Kostas Bartsokas](https://kostasbartsokas.com/) will examine how typographic texture changes in an era where legibility rules give way to creativity in the shift from text to screen; and [Liza Enebeis](https://www.loveliza.nl/) will touch upon the boundaries of experimentation, behavior, tools, materials, and collaboration to define the essence of an identity.

On the second day of the event, [Georg Seifert](https://www.instagram.com/schriftgestalt/) will host a workshop aimed at developing participants' Glyphs skills.

Türesay’s book, titled “[Being an Intellectual in the Ottoman Empire: Ebüzziya Tevfik (1849–1913) and His Time](https://www.peeters-leuven.be/detail.php?search_key=9789042945128&series_number_str=28&lang=en)”, adopts a socio-historical approach to trace the biography of Tevfik, a self-taught intellectual who embraced both Ottoman and Western culture. At the Common Alphabet Commission of the Turkic World meeting, organized by the Turkic Academy and the Turkish Language Association in Baku between September 9–11, 2024, and attended by officially appointed commission members from Turkic states, the Latin-based [common alphabet](https://tr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ortak_T%C3%BCrk_alfabesi) project first proposed in 1991 was comprehensively reviewed, and a consensus was [reached](https://tdk.gov.tr/icerik/duyurular/ortak-turk-alfabesine-iliskin-duyuru/) on a 34-letter “Common Turkic Alphabet”. Prof. Dr. Osman Mert, President of the Turkish Language Association, answered questions and shared details regarding the matter on the [Ekonomim](https://www.ekonomim.com/gundem/turkiyede-alfabe-degisecek-mi-turk-dil-kurumu-baskani-acikladi-haberi-767855) website.

629.title: A sans-serif for the needs of the 21st century: Zed
629.summary: Typotheque type foundry announced their new typeface Zed, which they describe as “a sans-serif for the needs of the twenty-first century.” The foundry states that most twentieth-century sans-serif typefaces compromise on design, whereas Zed was developed using the latest research on which letterforms are most easily…
629.content:
Typotheque type foundry announced their new typeface [Zed](https://www.typotheque.com/blog/zed-a-sans-for-the-needs-of-21century), which they describe as “a sans-serif for the needs of the twenty-first century.” The foundry states that most twentieth-century sans-serif typefaces compromise on design, whereas Zed was developed using the latest research on which letterforms are most easily read by the widest audience, thus directly addressing this shortcoming with different text and display versions. The foundry [tested](https://www.typotheque.com/articles/designing-fonts-with-low-vision-readers-in-mind) Zed with the help of visually impaired readers and worked with language communities and local designers around the world. Additionally, Zed was awarded a [Gold European Design Award](https://x.com/typotheque/status/1798994593394106378). 🇬🇧

755.title: Monotype’s “Content Credentials” initiative
755.summary: Bryan Comeau from Monotype announced that the company will adopt the “Content Credentials” initiative in the coming years, which is based on the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) standard that documents content provenance and editing history to help reduce the spread of misleading information…
755.content:
Bryan Comeau from Monotype [announced](https://www.monotype.com/resources/expertise/generating-trust-safeguarding-authenticity-typography) that the company will adopt the “[Content Credentials](https://contentcredentials.org/)” initiative in the coming years, which is based on the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) standard that documents content provenance and editing history to help reduce the spread of misleading information online. In doing so, the company aims to strengthen the credibility of digital assets and contribute to a more trustworthy and transparent online environment by addressing the challenges of creating and trusting digital media in the era of generative AI. Reactions to Monotype’s initiative were not long in coming. In a [post](https://twitter.com/arabictype/status/1772713336183889998), Kris Sowersby of Klim Type Foundry wondered how they would realistically handle this, noting that Monotype cannot yet reliably detect pirated typefaces sold on MyFonts. Nadine Chahine [stated](https://x.com/arabictype/status/1772713336183889998?s=20) that Monotype had sent out a newsletter about Futura Now where the entire text was about Avenir, remarking that they should get their own house in order first. 🇬🇧

567.title: Phil Baines has passed away.
567.summary: Prof. Phil Baines, a faculty member at Central Saint Martins (University of the Arts London) who made a name for himself with his work as a graphic designer, author, and educator, has passed away. After graduating from St Martin’s School of Art, Baines taught as a visiting lecturer in the 1980s and began working…
567.content:
Prof. Phil Baines, a faculty member at Central Saint Martins (University of the Arts London) who made a name for himself with his work as a graphic designer, author, and educator, [has passed away](https://www.arts.ac.uk/colleges/central-saint-martins/stories/professor-phil-baines-1958-2024). After graduating from St Martin’s School of Art, Baines taught as a visiting lecturer in the 1980s and began working full-time in 1991 at what was newly renamed Central Saint Martins; he was made a professor in 2006 for his contributions to the discipline. Turning the vernacular almost into a vocation and frequently leading walking tours in London to explore local lettering, Baines co-curated the [Central Lettering Record](https://collections.arts.ac.uk/collections/clr;jsessionid=6E09E68F344CA5896CF5CC1AA078A40E) at Central Saint Martins alongside Catherine Dixon. He had also been invited to conduct a seminar and workshop at the 13th edition of the [Grafist](http://grafist.org/project/grafist-13) event, held between October 2–17, 2009.

Adidas, the official apparel supplier of Turkey for the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games, prepared a special collection to be worn by Turkish athletes. [According to information provided by Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/spor/adidastan-paris-2024-olimpiyatlari-icin-turkiyeye-ozel-koleksiyon/3196525), the word “Türkiye” on the collection was set in a new typeface. When the jersey is examined, in addition to an overall disharmony between the letters, anatomical issues are evident in the letters Y and E. Additionally, positioning diacritics below the cap line—a practice we discussed extensively and emphasized as incorrect under the subheading “Lowercase Fetishism” in [the first part of our “Typographic Errors with Examples” series](https://medium.com/tipografi/%C3%B6rneklerle-tipografik-hatalar-b%C3%B6l%C3%BCm-1-9e4977b0188f)—is present in this example as well.

308.content:
Within the scope of the [2025 Gerard Unger Scholarship](https://www.type-together.com/2025-gerard-unger-scholarship-results), this year’s merit award was presented to [Yaprak Buse Çağlar](https://www.instagram.com/typolea/) for the typeface [Aksan](https://esadtype.esad-amiens.fr/aksan/), which she designed at EsadType. Designed to cover many languages using the Latin alphabet, Aksan draws inspiration from the Turkish Alphabet Reform, blending powerful visual references of the past with today's design sensibility.

The main award of the scholarship was won by Manau Quellec with the type family [Newz](https://esadtype.esad-amiens.fr/newz/), developed under the mentorship of Sébastien Morlighem during his studies at Ésad Amiens. In the competition, where 47 designers from 16 different countries participated with a total of 49 type designs, TypeTogether co-founder Veronika Burian stated that Newz demonstrated strong potential in terms of conceptuality, execution, and craftsmanship quality, noting that it is a versatile and powerful type family especially for publications. José Scaglione expressed his praise with the words, “It looks so good it makes me want to get into publishing!”

309.title: Manutius’s first edition printed in italic type sold for a record price!
309.summary: A copy of Publius Vergilius Maro’s Opera from 1501, offered for sale at the auction of Bibliotheca Brookeriana, found a buyer for a record price of $1,041,400. Printed by Aldus Manutius (1449–1515), the work is known not only as the first book in history printed in italic type, but also for introducing the pocket…
309.content:
A copy of Publius Vergilius Maro’s Opera from 1501, offered for sale at the auction of Bibliotheca Brookeriana, [found](https://www.sothebys.com/en/buy/auction/2025/bibliotheca-brookeriana-a-renaissance-library-the-aldine-collection-n-z/vergilius-opera-venice-aldo-manuzio-1501?utm_source=chatgpt.com) a buyer for a record price of $1,041,400. Printed by Aldus Manutius (1449–1515), the work is known not only as the first book in history printed in italic type, but also for introducing the *pocket classics* format to the publishing world. The italic type designed by Francesco Griffo, inspired by humanist cursive scripts, revolutionized the typographic approach of the era and served as a model for italic typefaces used in subsequent centuries. In this respect, the work holds an important place in terms of both printing history and typography.

312.title: Alembert and the influence of the writing masters
312.summary: Another design process is about Alembert, designed by Jean François Porchez for the thirtieth anniversary of Typofonderie… In his article, Porchez highlights the influence of seventeenth-century French writing masters (maîtres écrivains) and explains how historical script styles like Bâtarde and Coulée are…
312.content:
Another design process is about [Alembert](https://typofonderie.com/gazette/alembert-and-the-influence-of-the-maitres-ecrivains#fn1), designed by Jean François Porchez for the thirtieth anniversary of [Typofonderie](https://typofonderie.com/)… In his article, Porchez highlights the influence of seventeenth-century French writing masters (*maîtres écrivains*) and explains how historical script styles like *Bâtarde* and *Coulée* are reinterpreted through contemporary typography. Alembert was created through a combination of digital tools and hand-drawing techniques, offering a more fluid and warm aesthetic compared to the classic Anglaise style. Thus, the typeface stands out as an original design bringing together both historical heritage and modern typographic needs.

☞ Used in France and its surroundings—especially Burgundy—in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, **Bâtarde** is a script style derived from blackletter, featuring more ornate and fluid lines. Coulée, on the other hand, is a semi-formal script style used in France in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries that provided speed and ease in daily life. By the nineteenth century, these styles gradually gave way to Anglaise (Copperplate, English Roundhand), which developed in England.

318.content:
John Hudson [explores](https://www.tiro.com/articles/beneventan) the contradictory relationship between writing and forgetfulness through the *Beneventan* script, developed at the Benedictine Abbey of Monte Cassino. Drawing from the story of Theuth and Thutmose in Plato’s *Phaedrus* dialogue, he draws attention to the notion that writing, rather than strengthening memory, might make it lazy and prevent truly comprehending knowledge. In addition, the article mentions contemporary examples that revive the Beneventan script style, such as Ryoichi Tsunekawa’s “Agedage Beneventan” and Lazar Dimitrijević’s “Cal Beneventan Minuscule”.

340.title: Order to return to Times New Roman
340.summary: The US Department of State announced in a memo dated December 9, 2025, that it is returning to Times New Roman for official correspondence. The Department claimed that Calibri—which had been chosen during the Biden era on the grounds of offering higher readability for individuals with dyslexia and visual…
340.content:
The US Department of State [announced](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/dec/10/trump-times-new-roman-font-return-state-department) in a memo dated December 9, 2025, that it is returning to Times New Roman for official correspondence. The Department claimed that Calibri—which had been chosen during the Biden era on the grounds of offering higher readability for individuals with dyslexia and visual impairments—undermined institutional seriousness. Marco Rubio, who proposed the change, stated that abandoning Calibri would eliminate yet another wasteful DEIA (inclusive practices initiated across many areas during the Biden era) program.

A response was not long in coming from Lucas de Groot, who designed Calibri for Microsoft in 2004. Countering the *waste* argument with an unemotional [statement](https://www.instagram.com/p/DSIRAvGDNdc/) grounded entirely in legibility, screen technology, and technical shortcomings, de Groot emphasized that Times New Roman was designed not for digital screens, but for newspaper printing where ink bleeds into paper, and that it creates visual noise on modern screens, hindering readability. Drawing attention to technical carelessness in the digital version—particularly inconsistent spacing in uppercase letters that undermines a professional appearance—the designer stated that this decision takes the administration not only into the past, but also in a direction that is technically and functionally inferior.

341.title: Seoul’s transit network transitions to a new type system after forty years.

341.content:
The first major visual communication and wayfinding overhaul in forty years is beginning across Seoul’s public transit system. The new type system to be used across the entire network, from subways to buses, is based on the [Seoul Arim](https://www.printmag.com/type-tuesday/latin-hangul-visual-harmony-seoul-metro-type-system/) type family, developed through a collaborative effort between Dutch July Type and Korea-based Tlab. Uniting Latin and Hangul characters under a single cohesive structure, Seoul Arim offers both a calm and humane tone through its balanced proportions, open counters, and low contrast that enhance legibility. Seoul Arim will begin to be used throughout the entire transit network in 2026.

342.title: Fran Sans: The typeface keeping San Francisco’s disappearing typography alive

342.content:
Developed by Emily Sneddon, [Fran Sans](https://emilysneddon.com/fran-sans-essay) is a new typeface inspired by the LCD destination panels of San Francisco’s light rail system. Utilizing the fixed segments and small grid layout of the boards, the typeface demonstrates to the designer how constraints shape the creative process, while also helping preserve a disappearing typographic heritage. Comprising three members—*Solid, Tile*, and *Panel*—Sneddon aims with Fran Sans to revive the analog and slightly gritty typographic aesthetic in the digital realm, as the original boards will be replaced with LED screens and this visual language will be lost.
