343.title: Generational typographic attitudes in Monotype’s report
343.summary: The report titled “Fonts, Feels & Reels: Generational Attitudes Toward Typography,” published by Monotype in collaboration with Censuswide, reveals that typography directly influences user perception in digital communication. According to the research conducted with 12,000 participants from six countries, 69% of…
343.content:
The report titled “[Fonts, Feels & Reels: Generational Attitudes Toward Typography](https://www.monotype.com/generational-attitudes-to-type-survey),” published by Monotype in collaboration with Censuswide, reveals that typography directly influences user perception in digital communication. According to the research conducted with 12,000 participants from six countries, 69% of respondents consider typeface selection important when creating content. Even more striking is that 78% of participants stated that distinctive and well-chosen typefaces increase engagement on social media. Additionally, 65% of participants believe that the right typeface ensures message clarity and comprehensibility. On the brand perception side, 52% of Millennials state that typeface choice directly shapes their trust and loyalty toward a brand.

Examining these quantitative data presented by the report within the context of design practice and user psychology, Charles Nix [interpreted](https://www.fastcompany.com/91445670/a-new-generation-requires-font-sophistication-and-more) the findings through Gen Z’s forms of digital expression. Nix notes that Gen Z and Millennials position typography not merely as a tool for conveying text, but as a primary form of self-expression replacing handwriting. While handwriting usage declines with digitalization, digital typography filling this void transforms into a vehicle reflecting emotional tone for younger generations. However, the limited font options offered by current social media platforms fall short of meeting this need for *authenticity*. According to the report, 76% of Gen Z turn to off-platform design tools when creating content due to these constraints. The article emphasizes that brands should not overlook this typographic awareness, as the right typographic choice is a strategic element that directly increases engagement.

345.title: Adoption of variable fonts falls behind expectations!
345.summary: Although there is great interest in variable fonts, which provide both flexibility and efficiency by bringing all the diversity of a type family—such as weight, width, and style—into a single file, actual adoption rates in projects remain well behind expectations. Type Network data shows that the share of variable…
345.content:
Although there is great interest in variable fonts, which provide both flexibility and efficiency by bringing all the diversity of a type family—such as weight, width, and style—into a single file, actual adoption rates in projects remain well behind expectations. [Type Network data](https://typenetwork.com/articles/enthusiasm-for-variable-fonts-outpace-adoption) shows that the share of variable fonts in paid licensing remains below even 1%. The primary reason for this situation lies not in technical shortcomings, but in the economic barriers of licensing models. While designers generally prefer to purchase the individual static styles required for a project, the high pricing of variable fonts covering the entire family negatively affects purchasing decisions. Indeed, in subscription systems where additional costs are eliminated (such as Adobe Fonts, etc.), usage is seen to increase proportionally with library availability. Therefore, the real obstacle standing in the way of structural advantages such as flexible interface design, performance, and accessibility is not a designer adaptation problem, but market dynamics…

347.title: History of the invisible mark: From Capitulum to Pilcrow
347.summary: Authoring an essay on the paragraph mark (pilcrow, ¶), Jonathan Hoefler touches upon how this mark—whose origins trace back to the Latin Capitulum, meaning chapter—reached its contemporary form through visual metamorphosis over the centuries. The text reveals that the mark actually has nothing to do with the P in the…
347.content:
Authoring an essay on the paragraph mark (pilcrow, ¶), Jonathan Hoefler [touches upon](https://www.typography.com/blog/pilcrow-capitulum) how this mark—whose origins trace back to the Latin *Capitulum*, meaning *chapter*—reached its contemporary form through visual metamorphosis over the centuries.

The text reveals that the mark actually has nothing to do with the P in the word paragraph; its original shape was a letter *C*, and the vertical strokes added to it extended downward over time, creating the illusion of a *reverse P* during the Renaissance. Serving as a powerful example of the lasting effect of scribal practice on the shapes of glyphs, this mark—usually *invisible* in modern applications—continues to remain a functional challenge for type designers.

---

348.title: The debate over copyright protection for fonts is back on the agenda
348.summary: Matthew Butterick argues that the copyright strategies the type industry has long relied upon may not be as legally sound as presumed. Following the Laatz v. Zazzle lawsuit, Butterick brings up the reality that fonts are not protected by copyright as visual design under US law. Reminding readers that the industry has…
348.content:
Matthew Butterick [argues](https://matthewbutterick.com/chron/the-copyrightability-of-fonts-revisited.html) that the copyright strategies the type industry has long relied upon may not be as legally sound as presumed. Following the *Laatz v. Zazzle* lawsuit, Butterick brings up the reality that fonts are not protected by copyright as visual design under US law. Reminding readers that the industry has attempted to overcome this loophole by classifying and registering fonts as computer software, Butterick emphasizes that this approach does not provide absolute assurance in the eyes of the courts. In his view, in the current environment of legal uncertainty, the most rational strategy for independent designers is not filing lawsuits, but establishing quality market relationships…

349.content:
Following the sale of Hoefler & Co. to Monotype in 2021, and with designs like Gotham *now appearing detached from their origins*, Doug Wilson penned a comprehensive [article](https://frerejones.com/blog/designing-gotham). The article conveys from a technical and historical perspective how Gotham, which began in 2000 as a search for identity for GQ magazine, was derived from local New York signage. A great read to learn the true story of Gotham.

350.title: On balance and progression in type design
350.summary: Typofonderie published Evert Bloemsma’s 2000 article questioning the search for balance and progression in type design. Bloemsma discusses in technical detail how the typographic color of letterforms can be consistently maintained across the different weights of a type family, and the importance of aesthetic rhythm…
350.content:
Typofonderie published Evert Bloemsma’s 2000 [article](https://typofonderie.com/gazette/looking-for-balance-and-progression) questioning the search for balance and progression in type design. Bloemsma discusses in technical detail how the typographic color of letterforms can be consistently maintained across the different weights of a type family, and the importance of aesthetic rhythm perceived by the eye beyond mechanical construction.

Dutch graphic designer and type designer Evert Bloemsma (1958–2005) studied at the Arnhem Academy of Art. Focusing on functionality in his type designs and pursuing forms suited to the needs of the era, the designer is renowned for his typefaces *FF Balance*, *FF Cocon*, *FF Avance*, and *FF Legato*.

351.title: American Sign Museum’s gold leaf collection
351.summary: “Selling a gold leaf job is much easier when you can show your client what can be done, rather than just telling them.” Published on the occasion of the American Sign Museum’s 25th anniversary, the book brings to light gold leaf samples of critical importance to typography history and sign painting. Dating from the…
351.content:
> “Selling a gold leaf job is much easier when you can show your client what can be done, rather than just telling them.”

Published on the occasion of the American Sign Museum’s 25th anniversary, the book brings to light gold leaf samples of critical importance to typography history and sign painting. Dating from the late 19th to early 20th century, these rare pieces document the relationship letter anatomy establishes with reverse glass techniques and light, through benchmark works crafted by masters such as Raymond J. LeBlanc and George C. Brooke. With this publication, the museum turns the artisans’ strategy of providing visual evidence over verbal explanation, along with nearly forgotten material knowledge, into a resource for contemporary type designers.

356.content:
The Type Directors Club, the world’s leading typography organization, [announced](https://tdc.org/news/2025-ade-hogue-beatrice-warde-and-tdc-scholarships-announced/) this year’s winners of its student scholarship programs. The Adé Hogue Scholarship, sponsored by Monotype in memory of designer Adé Hogue, who passed away at a young age in 2021, was shared between Katherine Ispache from the California Institute of the Arts and Charitssa Stone from the Yale School of Art.

The winner of the scholarship awarded in memory of Beatrice Warde, a key figure in typographic history and the TDC’s first female member, was Siyun Li from the School of Visual Arts. In addition, general merit scholarships were awarded to undergraduate students studying at institutions such as Rhode Island School of Design, ArtCenter College of Design, Parsons, and Bauhaus-University Weimar who demonstrated outstanding talent in the fields of typographic form, composition, and design criticism.

357.title: Google Sans and Google Sans are now open source
357.summary: Google is making its iconic type family Google Sans and its variable font version Google Sans Flex—which allows designers to make adjustments along six different axes—open source. This move means that the type family can now be used freely and at no cost across the entire digital world, not just in Google products.…
357.content:
Google is [making](https://design.google/library/google-sans-flex-font) its iconic type family [Google Sans](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Google+Sans) and its variable font version [Google Sans Flex](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Google+Sans+Flex)—which allows designers to make adjustments along six different axes—open source. This move means that the type family can now be used freely and at no cost across the entire digital world, not just in Google products. Born out of necessity following the logo change in 2015 and evolving over time to solve many challenges from small-size legibility to coding, this family aims to create a more consistent and accessible web experience.

405.title: Riccardo Olocco was at ISType.
405.summary: Riccardo Olocco gave a talk at Salt Galata on Thursday, October 30, 2025, as part of ISType Mono. Addressing the evolution of typography from the Renaissance to the present day, Olocco provided an overview of type design of the period, focusing on the search for original forms spanning from Gutenberg’s DK type to…
405.content:
[Riccardo Olocco](https://www.riccardolocco.com/) gave a talk at Salt Galata on Thursday, October 30, 2025, as part of [ISType Mono](https://istype.com/riccardo-olocco/). Addressing the evolution of typography from the Renaissance to the present day, Olocco provided an overview of type design of the period, focusing on the search for original forms spanning from Gutenberg’s DK type to Jenson’s Roman types. He also introduced several contemporary type designs directly based on the revival of Renaissance models or inspired by them.

Working as a type designer at [CAST Type Foundry](https://www.c-a-s-t.com/), Olocco completed his doctoral studies at the University of Reading, focusing on 15th-century Venetian Roman types. In 2022, he co-authored the book “Designing Type Revivals” with Michele Patanè. He taught typography at the University of Bolzano and carried out work in Milan and various cities across Northern Italy. He is also a member of the *Nebiolo History Project*—which we also featured in our [May 2022](https://medium.com/tipografi/tipografi-haberleri-may%C4%B1s-2022-c258249bd466) and [August 2023](https://medium.com/tipografi/tipografi-b%C3%BClteni-a%C4%9Fustos-2023-5ee8b04702ec) bulletins.

407.content:
Odunpazarı Modern Museum (OMM) in Eskişehir is hosting the site-specific installation “[Calligraphic Wig](https://www.omm.art/tr/sergi/calligraphic-wig)” by Berlin-based Romanian artist Daniel Knorr between October 25, 2025, and March 21, 2026. The forms born from production glitches observed by Knorr in plastic recycling factories in Hong Kong transform into organic structures reminiscent of unknown alphabets. Questioning the boundary between industrial production and aesthetics by coating some pieces with automotive paint colors from the 1970s to the present, the artist leaves others in their raw state, making the randomness and transformative capacity of the material visible.

413.content:
With the *Adaline* project, Daybreak Studio [demonstrates](https://www.daybreak.studio/writing/adaline-typography) an unconventional approach to web typography. 415.title: The NY Sign Museum preserves the city’s typographic richness.
415.summary: “We save these signs not just because they look cool, but because they mean something to us, to New Yorkers, and to the community.” David Barnett, co-founder of Noble Signs and the New York Sign Museum Charlotte Beach recounts how the Noble Signs initiative, founded under the leadership of David Barnett and Mac…
415.content:
> “We save these signs not just because they look cool, but because they mean something to us, to New Yorkers, and to the community.”

> David Barnett, co-founder of Noble Signs and the New York Sign Museum

Charlotte Beach [recounts](https://www.printmag.com/design-culture/the-ny-sign-museum/) how the *Noble Signs* initiative, founded under the leadership of David Barnett and Mac Pohanka, transformed into a museum with the mission of preserving New York’s visual memory. In addition to more than 150 vintage signs reflecting the city’s street culture, the New York Sign Museum houses a rich collection of thermometers, calendars, matchbooks used for advertising by local businesses, and 400 shopping bags from the 1970s and 1980s. The museum aims to pass on the city’s typographic heritage to future generations and bring traditional sign-making methods together with contemporary design practice.

> “What does a designer’s story look like when it also encompasses a life?”

The untold story of Czech designer Clara Istlerová (b. 1944) comes to light with the book “[A Life Among Letters](https://www.itsnicethat.com/articles/clara-istlerov%C3%A1s-ane%C5%BEka-mina%C5%99ikov%C3%A1-a-life-among-letters-publication-project-081025)” by [Anežka Minařiková](https://anezkaminarikova.com/). Bringing together interviews, archival research, and personal anecdotes with Istlerová—who stood out as the sole female member of the *Typo&* collective active in the Czech design scene during the 1970s—Minařiková presents a pocket-sized monograph. The book can be purchased from [Inventory Press](https://www.inventorypress.com/product/a-life-among-letters).

421.title: Website launched for typography classic “Printing Types”
421.summary: A comprehensive online edition of American printer, typographer, and historian Daniel Berkeley Updike’s (1860–1941) two-volume classic of the typography world, “Printing Types: Their History, Forms & Use”, has been presented online by Nicholas Rougeux, enriched with original specimens. 421.content:
A comprehensive online edition of American printer, typographer, and historian Daniel Berkeley Updike’s (1860–1941) two-volume classic of the typography world, “[Printing Types: Their History, Forms & Use](https://www.c82.net/printing-types/)”, has been presented online by Nicholas Rougeux, enriched with original specimens. Examining the printing tradition in Europe and America from the 15th to the 20th century, the historical evolution of type design, geographical differences, and contributions to the graphic arts, the work was one of the first historical studies to systematically address the development of typefaces.

425.content:
Aimed at revitalizing endangered and underrepresented writing systems, [The Donald Knuth & Charles Bigelow Type Design Incubator](https://www.kbitype.org/) (KBI) program has begun accepting applications. Unicode-compliant and containing more than three thousand characters, the typeface was developed in accordance with the key recommendations of the American Mathematical Society using a professional character set to be fully compatible with LaTeX. Furthermore, it is offered under the Open Font License (OFL) and can be downloaded and used free of charge.

387.title: Tausend: An innovative approach to the geometric grotesque tradition
387.summary: The article on the design process of Tausend, a new sans serif type collection designed by Christoph Koeberlin and Gabriel Richter, explores the collection’s starting point and development stages. The story begins with a characteristic letter “a” that emerged during Koeberlin’s design of Tresor. With type designer…
387.content:
The [article](https://fontwerk.com/en/text/tausend) on the design process of [Tausend](https://fontwerk.com/en/fonts/tausend-collection), a new sans serif type collection designed by Christoph Koeberlin and Gabriel Richter, explores the collection’s starting point and development stages. The story begins with a characteristic letter “a” that emerged during Koeberlin’s design of [Tresor](https://www.nan.xyz/fonts/nan-tresor/). With type designer [Gabriel Richter](https://fontwerk.com/en/designers/gabriel-richter) joining the project—where the structural features of this letter formed the collection’s DNA—modernity, dynamism, and a fresh interpretation of the geometric grotesque tradition are added. Tausend is described as a powerful family not only aesthetically, but also functionally. Its support for the DIN 91379 standard, which meets the official requirements of many languages including EU countries, makes it a reliable choice for institutions and brands. While the type family offers a wide range of styles with different typefaces such as Plakat, Soft, Stencil, and Shaded, adaptations provided in optical sizes promise high legibility from small text to large headlines.

390.title: New research on generative neural networks in typography
390.summary: The doctoral research by Filip Paldia examines the potential of AI-based generative neural networks in the field of typography. By highlighting the limitations of methods used in type design, Paldia proposes new datasets, representations, and tools that can overcome these constraints. The study offers contributions on…
390.content:
The [doctoral research](https://lttrface.com/doctoral-thesis) by Filip Paldia examines the potential of AI-based generative neural networks in the field of typography. By highlighting the limitations of methods used in type design, Paldia proposes new datasets, representations, and tools that can overcome these constraints. The study offers contributions on both theoretical and practical levels by systematically classifying existing AI-based font projects in the literature. It also highlights the creative potential of artificial intelligence in typography through curated font datasets and sample use cases.

391.title: Typography in interface design
391.summary: In his article written in 2016, Ariel Salminen explains the role of typography in interface design, legibility, and the principles of making good typographic choices. Emphasizing that text is in fact the fundamental component of user interfaces, the article addresses both the functional and aesthetic aspects of…
391.content:
In his [article](https://arielsalminen.com/2016/typography-for-user-interfaces/) written in 2016, Ariel Salminen explains the role of typography in interface design, legibility, and the principles of making good typographic choices. Emphasizing that text is in fact the fundamental component of user interfaces, the article addresses both the functional and aesthetic aspects of typography. Characteristics such as easily distinguishable letters, legibility across different screen sizes and resolutions, adequate spacing, low contrast, and a large x-height are listed as essentials of a good typeface for interface design.

392.summary: Nick Shinn recounts the process of naming typefaces through personal experiences and anecdotes. He emphasizes that the names of typefaces are determined sometimes by chance, and sometimes through deliberate choices. For example, he used his own name for the typefaces Shinn Sans and Shinn Gothic, took the name Beaufort…
392.content:
Nick Shinn [recounts](https://shinntype.com/on-the-naming-of-fonts/) the process of naming typefaces through personal experiences and anecdotes. He emphasizes that the names of typefaces are determined sometimes by chance, and sometimes through deliberate choices. For example, he used his own name for the typefaces *Shinn Sans* and *Shinn Gothic*, took the name *Beaufort* from Beaufort Street in Toronto, while the name *Pratt Nova* was inspired by David Pratt, the art director of *The Globe and Mail* newspaper.

394.title: When brand typefaces go open source

394.content:
According to [an article by Sarah Daily](https://design.google/library/open-source-custom-fonts-google) from Google Design, many organizations are sharing custom typefaces developed for their brands as open source. Typefaces such as IBM Plex, Mona Sans, and Atkinson Hyperlegible not only contribute to brand identity, but also provide solutions to design challenges like legibility, accessibility, and multilingual use. Open source licensed typefaces eliminate licensing costs while enabling contributions from independent designers. Thus, typography becomes a shared design language that both strengthens the identity of organizations and can be shared on a global scale.

396.title: Why did Spotify hire a typographer?
396.summary: In her article written for Creative Bloq, Rosie Hilder explores the reasons why Spotify hired a typographer. As reported in the piece, Spotify recognizes that within interface design and its design system Encore, typography is no longer a side task, but a standalone discipline that requires continuous maintenance and…
396.content:
In her [article](https://www.creativebloq.com/design/fonts-typography/why-spotify-hired-a-dedicated-typographer) written for Creative Bloq, Rosie Hilder explores the reasons why Spotify hired a typographer. As reported in the piece, Spotify recognizes that within interface design and its design system *Encore*, typography is no longer a *side task*, but a standalone discipline that requires continuous maintenance and expertise. In the article, [Bianca Berning](https://bberning.com/), who works at Spotify, notes that typography is critical not only visually, but also to ensure that text reaches the user accurately, legibly, and consistently across different languages, cultures, and platforms. Hilder also points out that while artificial intelligence provides technical support in typography, this work cannot be fully automated, and human experience and oversight remain indispensable.

397.title: A previously unknown ancient language discovered in Turkey.
397.summary: Clay tablets found during excavations at the ancient Hittite capital of Hattusa in Çorum have brought to light an ancient language unknown until now. Named “Kalasmaic,” this language is believed to belong to the Kalašma people who lived approximately three thousand years ago. While the discovery holds the potential to…
397.content:
Clay tablets found during excavations at the ancient Hittite capital of Hattusa in Çorum have [brought to light](https://gazeteoksijen.com/o2/turkiyede-daha-once-bilinmeyen-antik-bir-dil-kesfedildi-252630) an ancient language unknown until now. Named “Kalasmaic,” this language is believed to belong to the Kalašma people who lived approximately three thousand years ago. While the discovery holds the potential to fill gaps in Bronze Age Near Eastern history, researchers predict that the number of languages identified on the tablets—currently standing at five—could reach into the thirties.

398.content:
In a [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wHv4uxzjyHo) published on his YouTube channel, Mustafa B. Bozkurt traces the evolution of writing through a chronological journey. The video examines how writing evolved from simple memory aids such as early notches and pictograms into more complex systems through logograms and phoneticization. By also recounting the story of new writing systems that emerged in different geographies, it summarizes the journey of writing up to the present day.

399.content:
Murat Ertaş, President of the Erzurum Branch of the Turkish Language and Literature Association, [advocates](https://www.haber3.com/guncel/29-harflik-alfabe-yetersiz-deyip-4-yeni-harf-onerdi-haberi-6237544) for adding four new letters to the alphabet, arguing that the current 29-letter Turkish alphabet falls short of reflecting the phonetic and lexical richness of our language. According to Ertaş, the alphabet should expand to 33 letters with these additions, and local or ancient words forgotten over time should be *revived*.

403.title: New book: “The Letters of Sakarya”
403.summary: The book “The Letters of Sakarya: In Pursuit of Commercial Artists and Sign Paintings” by one of our editors, Murat Ertürk, has been published by Değişim Yayınları with the support of the Sakarya Chamber of Commerce and Industry. The product of seven years of research, the book documents the forgotten legacy of…
403.content:
The book “[The Letters of Sakarya: In Pursuit of Commercial Artists and Sign Paintings](https://www.kitapyurdu.com/kitap/sakaryanin-harfleri-ticari-ressamlarin-ve-firca-yazilarinin-izinde/732750.html&filter_name=sakaryan%C4%B1n+harfleri)” by one of our editors, [Murat Ertürk](https://www.muraterturk.com/), has been published by Değişim Yayınları with the support of the [Sakarya Chamber of Commerce and Industry](https://www.satso.org.tr/). The product of seven years of research, the book documents the forgotten legacy of commercial artists active in Sakarya from the 1940s to the 1990s through more than 650 photographs and archival documents. Featuring information and documents compiled from oral interviews conducted with first-degree relatives and witnesses, the first section of the book sheds light on commercial artists and the intergenerational transmission of the local lettering and illustration tradition extending into design and advertising. The second section, featuring photographic contributions by Ali Yıldırım, showcases the city’s typographic richness across six categories, ranging from title plates and industrial zone signs to shop signs and warning plaques.

336.title: “Sampling Type”
336.summary: Consisting of a web page and risograph-printed posters, Franzi Häußner’s project titled “Sampling Type” questions how typefaces bearing traces of the past are reproduced while calling for a critical approach to the use of sources, presenting interviews conducted with designers in both digital and physical formats.…
336.content:
Consisting of a web page and risograph-printed posters, [Franzi Häußner](https://franzihaeussner.de/)’s project titled “[Sampling Type](https://samplingtype.xyz/)” questions how typefaces bearing traces of the past are reproduced while calling for a critical approach to the use of sources, presenting interviews conducted with designers in both digital and physical formats. Inspired by the concept of “sampling” in music, the project investigates creative ways to reuse typefaces. Developed as part of a master’s thesis at [Konstanz University of Applied Sciences](https://www.htwg-konstanz.de/) (HTWG), the project was exhibited at the [Werkschau](https://werkschau-konstanz.de/) in Konstanz this past February.

366.title: When is a type design finished?
366.summary: “Finishing a type design is more like deciding to stop.” In her article questioning the idea of completely finishing a typeface, Flavia Zimbardi examines elements such as flow, resistance, and collaboration within the design process, emphasizing how the concept of completion can restrict creativity. It is a compelling…
366.content:
> “Finishing a type design is more like deciding to stop.”

In her [article](https://contraforma.substack.com/p/is-finishing-fonts-a-lie) questioning the idea of completely finishing a typeface, Flavia Zimbardi examines elements such as flow, resistance, and collaboration within the design process, emphasizing how the concept of *completion* can restrict creativity. It is a compelling resource for understanding contemporary production practices for type foundries and type designers.

367.title: The future of the type industry
367.summary: “We are (…) highly specialised, modern craftspeople whose typefaces have worked smoothly across digital platforms, apps, software environments, and operating systems for more than three decades.” Kris Sowersby Flavia Zimbardi’s piece, which addresses the uncertainties facing the typography sector through the panels of…
367.content:
> “We are (…) highly specialised, modern craftspeople whose typefaces have worked smoothly across digital platforms, apps, software environments, and operating systems for more than three decades.”

> Kris Sowersby

Flavia Zimbardi’s [piece](https://contraforma.substack.com/p/can-we-still-build-a-future-in-type), which addresses the uncertainties facing the typography sector through the panels of the *Font Business* conference held last June, is also noteworthy. In her article, Zimbardi notes that concerns about designers’ ability to sustain their careers, navigate changing conditions, and cope with narrowing opportunities take center stage. While the article emphasizes that type design has historically required a patient and methodical production process, it points out that today multifaceted pressures such as economic fluctuations, wars, and corporate dominance are straining the industry.

The type foundry sector, being a niche field, is finding it increasingly difficult to turn a profit and find inspiration, while major distributors and tech giants retain control of the market. (While on the subject, let us also recall our [article](https://medium.com/tipografi/yaz%C4%B1-end%C3%BCstrisinde-tekelle%C5%9Fme-f100fe18760b) where we touched upon monopolization debates in the type industry.) Although artificial intelligence offers speed and cost advantages in production, it shapes perception by redefining *acceptable* conventions. In this environment, individual efforts fall short; collaboration and resource sharing are no longer just an option, but a survival strategy.

---

368.title: The joys and challenges of screen typography
368.summary: Focusing on the tension between the aesthetic ideals of typography in the digital medium and its technological limitations, the article emphasizes that the necessity of adapting to different device sizes and browser settings makes it difficult to apply traditional print typography rules. It argues that both designers…
368.content:
Focusing on the tension between the aesthetic ideals of typography in the digital medium and its technological limitations, the [article](https://gwco.uk/journal/the-joys-and-pains-of-type-on-screen) emphasizes that the necessity of adapting to different device sizes and browser settings makes it difficult to apply traditional print typography rules. It argues that both designers and web developers must collaborate to bring the typography quality of the print world into the digital realm. It serves as a brief and practical introduction for those looking to produce legible and meticulously crafted text on screen.

369.title: Improving the loading speed of fonts on web pages

Recommending the use of modern font formats (WOFF/WOFF2), preloading, and CSS techniques such as font-display: swap, the article notes that limiting the…
369.content:
According to the [article](https://typetype.org/blog/web-font-optimization-the-key-to-instant-website-loading-speed/) published on the TypeType blog, properly optimizing web typefaces directly impacts page loading speed, user experience, and conversion rates. Recommending the use of modern font formats (WOFF/WOFF2), preloading, and CSS techniques such as `font-display: swap`, the article notes that limiting the number of typefaces used and removing unnecessary glyphs from files improves page performance.

370.title: Typography’s invisible power of persuasion
370.summary: Louise Sloper highlights that font choice—often relegated to the background in the industry—can actually quietly steer reader perception and decision-making processes. She grounds this argument in Errol Morris’s 2013 New York Times experiment, which measured the persuasive power on readers of the same text presented…
370.content:
Louise Sloper [highlights](https://magazine.shots.net/news/view/the-storytelling-superpower-of-typography) that font choice—often relegated to the background in the industry—can actually quietly steer reader perception and decision-making processes. She grounds this argument in Errol Morris’s 2013 New York Times experiment, which measured the persuasive power on readers of the same text presented in different typefaces. In the experiment, Baskerville was found to be more *believable* than Georgia, Helvetica, Comic Sans, and Trebuchet. Sloper also conveys that variable fonts and AI-powered typographic tools will broaden tone, persuasive power, and narrative possibilities in communication, making this impact even more pronounced in the future.

---

371.title: Typographic challenges of early Arabic printing
371.summary: In her article published by the American Printing History Association, Hala Auji highlights the technical and aesthetic challenges faced by Arabic printing. The fact that Arabic letters change shape according to their position within a word made it difficult for movable metal type printing to accommodate this…
371.content:
In her [article](https://printinghistory.org/challenges-of-early-arabic-printing/) published by the American Printing History Association, Hala Auji highlights the technical and aesthetic challenges faced by Arabic printing. The fact that Arabic letters change shape according to their position within a word made it difficult for movable metal type printing to accommodate this flexibility. Consequently, Arabic book printing remained a costly and limited field of production for a long time. According to Auji, despite these obstacles, printers developed creative solutions in typographic ornaments to preserve manuscript aesthetics. While debates surrounding Turkey’s 1928 Alphabet Reform are often conducted around the inability to read older works due to the script change, the technical difficulties brought about by printing processes should not be overlooked as an important factor.

372.title: The Didot family and the typographic ideal of the 19th century
372.summary: In his article addressing the rise of the Didot family, Michel Wlassikoff notes that the Didone style represented the industrial ideal of the nineteenth century through the aesthetic established by technical precision, high contrast, and hairline serifs. While discussing the relationship of this ideal to the cultural,…
372.content:
In his [article](https://typofonderie.com/gazette/didots-or-the-typographic-ideal-of-the-19th-century) addressing the rise of the Didot family, Michel Wlassikoff notes that the Didone style represented the industrial ideal of the nineteenth century through the aesthetic established by technical precision, high contrast, and hairline serifs. While discussing the relationship of this ideal to the cultural, economic, and technological transformations of the era, the article also evaluates the influence of the Didots' design approach on modern typography.

In this project, he collects vintage movable wood type, reworks it, and makes it available for use with modern printing techniques. Aiming to bring wood type into today’s design world while preserving its historical value…
373.content:
Daniel Swartz announced his project titled “[Rescuing Wood Type](https://hoosiertypeco.substack.com/p/rescuing-wood-type),” bringing wood type back to life. In this project, he collects vintage movable wood type, reworks it, and makes it available for use with modern printing techniques. Aiming to bring wood type into today’s design world while preserving its historical value and aesthetic characteristics, Swartz seeks to raise awareness about the preservation and reuse of wood type.

374.title: Typography debate over the Oval Office sign
374.summary: The script sign hung on Trump’s Oval Office door has received its share of criticism. Oliver Schöndorfer notes that the lettering is likely Shelley Script or English 111, and while attempting to appear elegant, it comes across as insecure and fails to deliver the claimed sense of luxury. Poor connections between…
374.content:
The script sign hung on Trump’s Oval Office door has received its share of criticism. [Oliver Schöndorfer](https://pimpmytype.com/oval-office-sign/) notes that the lettering is likely [Shelley Script](http://www.identifont.com/show?36G) or [English 111](http://www.identifont.com/show?260), and while attempting to appear elegant, it comes across as insecure and fails to deliver the claimed sense of luxury. Poor connections between letters, heavy strokes, and inconsistent spacing have turned it into gilded lettering that aims to showcase luxury but instead appears artificial and insecure. According to Schöndorfer, decorative fonts should be used with caution on signage, and materials and proportions must align with typography’s purpose.

---

375.title: On the female face of type with Alice Savoie
375.summary: In his interview with type designer Alice Savoie, François Chevret discusses typography’s relationship with gender, representation, and production culture. Savoie discusses how women designers have historically been rendered invisible, the efforts of contemporary type foundries to be more inclusive, and how she…
375.content:
In his interview with type designer Alice Savoie, François Chevret [discusses](https://tentation-du-regard.fr/une-femme-de-caracteres/) typography’s relationship with gender, representation, and production culture. Savoie discusses how women designers have historically been rendered invisible, the efforts of contemporary type foundries to be more inclusive, and how she navigates these balances in her own practice. The interview offers an in-depth look at the current standing of women’s labor in the field of typography, from the [Women in Type](https://www.women-in-type.com/) project—which we have also covered in our bulletins—to Savoie’s own production philosophy.

378.title: Union Gothic wins the election in New York.
378.summary: In the campaign identity of Zohran Mamdani, who was elected mayor of New York, the typeface Union Gothic by Matthew Hinders-Anderson—who made his entire type library free for non-commercial use—was used. 378.content:
In the [campaign identity](https://www.transition2025.com/) of Zohran Mamdani, who was elected mayor of New York, the typeface Union Gothic by Matthew Hinders-Anderson—who made his entire type library free for non-commercial use—was used. Throughout the campaign, [Union Gothic](https://wehtt.am/fonts/)’s simple, striking, and high-contrast aesthetic clearly set Mamdani’s communication apart. This choice stands out as a contemporary example of typographic selection, which has become one of the cornerstone elements of election campaign communication in the US over the past twenty years.

379.title: Rosetta Type Foundry’s variable font: Handjet
379.summary: Designed by David Březina, founder of Rosetta Type Foundry, the typeface Handjet pushes the boundaries of variable fonts using 23 basic elements. The process, which began in a design workshop in Brno with the motto “build all characters with a single element,” soon expanded with the addition of Latin, Cyrillic, Greek,…
379.content:
Designed by David Březina, founder of [Rosetta Type Foundry](https://rosettatype.com/), the typeface [Handjet](https://rosettatype.com/Handjet) [pushes](https://www.itsnicethat.com/articles/rosetta-type-foundry-handjet-graphic-design-140621) the boundaries of variable fonts using 23 basic elements. The process, which began in a design workshop in Brno with the motto “build all characters with a single element,” soon expanded with the addition of Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, and many other scripts. The standout feature of Handjet is that it offers seamless transitions between shapes and encompasses different weights, styles, and animation options within a single font. With support for Arabic, Armenian, Hebrew, and Korean, it also serves as an exemplar in multilingual design.

---

380.title: A new typeface inspired by 1970s Holborn
380.summary: Manchester-based type foundry F37 has announced its new typeface Holborn, inspired by London’s Holborn district in the 1970s. Drawing upon the storefront and signage aesthetics of the era, the typeface stands out with its strong geometric structure. Founder Rick Banks states that Holborn is not just a typeface, but a…
380.content:
Manchester-based type foundry F37 has announced its new typeface [Holborn](https://www.creativereview.co.uk/type-foundry-f37-releases-new-font-inspired-by-1970s-holborn/), inspired by London’s Holborn district in the 1970s. Drawing upon the storefront and signage aesthetics of the era, the typeface stands out with its strong geometric structure. Founder Rick Banks states that Holborn is not just a typeface, but a design project rooted in London’s visual history. Additionally, in a special book produced with Nomad Studio, the type foundry showcases the typeface by reinterpreting it across the signage of more than a hundred businesses. A wonderful study on how typefaces shape space!

---

381.title: Gotham’s new look
381.summary: Gotham had become synonymous with Obama’s 2007 presidential campaign and formed the foundation of the Obama Foundation’s identity. Collaborating with Monotype, Manual Creative aimed to inject new energy into Gotham while preserving its essence. This evolution resulted in the adoption of Gotham Condensed Bold as the…
381.content:
Gotham had become synonymous with Obama’s 2007 presidential campaign and formed the foundation of the Obama Foundation’s identity. Collaborating with Monotype, Manual Creative aimed to inject new energy into Gotham while preserving its essence. This evolution resulted in the adoption of [Gotham Condensed Bold](https://www.monotype.com/resources/case-studies/gotham-typeface-evolution-obama-foundation) as the primary benchmark and the development of three custom typefaces: *Gotham Inline* for sports communication, *Gotham Slab* reinforcing democratic themes, and *Gotham Stencil* symbolizing civic participation. Thus, Gotham aimed to establish a language carrying both consistency and diversity under a single roof.

---

382.title: A look at 2025 in the type industry
382.summary: In 2025, the type industry is shaped along the axis of tension between digital innovation and traditional craft. While variable font technologies blur the distinctions between sans and serif, increasing the use of flexible superfamilies, brands are turning to bespoke creations by independent designers rather than…
382.content:
In 2025, the type industry is shaped along the axis of tension between digital innovation and traditional craft. While variable font technologies blur the distinctions between sans and serif, increasing the use of flexible superfamilies, brands are turning to bespoke creations by independent designers rather than major type foundries to achieve authenticity in their corporate identities. As ethical and aesthetic debates sparked by artificial intelligence persist, a return to craftsmanship and revivals is gaining momentum as a reaction against digital aesthetics. A [useful guide](https://type-01.com/2025-in-overview-what-is-the-current-state-of-the-type-industry/) for an objective look at the world of type.

436.title: Comic Sans and the art of imperfection
436.summary: “Comic Sans wasn’t meant to start a revolution.” Even though Comic Sans has a bad reputation—which it never deserved—it actually served its intended design purpose quite well. In 1994, American type designer Vinnie Connare noticed Times New Roman being used in a speech balloon for Rover the dog in the Microsoft Bob…
436.content:
> “Comic Sans wasn’t meant to start a revolution.”

Even though Comic Sans has a bad reputation—which it never deserved—it actually served its intended design purpose quite well. In 1994, American type designer Vinnie Connare noticed Times New Roman being used in a speech balloon for Rover the dog in the Microsoft Bob software, thought that dogs don’t talk in Times New Roman, and designed the casual, friendly, and handwriting-like Comic Sans. [In her article, Danielle McClune](https://microsoft.design/articles/comic-sans-and-the-art-of-imperfection/) states that the imperfections of Comic Sans actually highlight its human and accessible qualities, which is why it holds a unique place in the design world.

439.title: A $30,000 bill from Monotype
439.summary: Monotype raised the annual license fee for Avenir, which a non-profit organization had been using for ten years, from $4,000 to $30,000. As justification, it cited font access by five employees and freelance designers, along with 150,000 monthly pageviews on the website, as a license violation. Furthermore, it…
439.content:
Monotype [raised](https://www.reddit.com/r/graphic_design/comments/1jqqlm6/monotype_just_hit_us_with_a_30000yr_font_license/?rdt=44913) the annual license fee for Avenir, which a non-profit organization had been using for ten years, from $4,000 to $30,000. As justification, it cited font access by five employees and freelance designers, along with 150,000 monthly pageviews on the website, as a *license violation*. Furthermore, it announced that if they do not accept the new fee, it will demand retroactive usage fees for the past ten years. The debates, sparked by [Grilli Type’s post on X](https://x.com/grillitype/status/1908232294029992270), brought the complexity of font licensing and Monotype’s aggressive policies back to the forefront. Debates over Monotype’s monopolization had been on the agenda before, and we had published an [article](https://medium.com/tipografi/yaz%C4%B1-end%C3%BCstrisinde-tekelle%C5%9Fme-f100fe18760b) on this topic.

258.content:
Elizabeth L. Eisenstein’s book “[The Printing Revolution in Early Modern Europe](https://www.iskultur.com.tr/erken-modern-avrupada-matbaa-devrimi.aspx)”, which examines the fifteenth-century printing revolution in the West in all its aspects, has been published by Türkiye İş Bankası Kültür Yayınları in a translation by Hamit Çalışkan. An abridged version of the work originally published in two volumes in 1979 under the title “The Printing Press as an Agent of Change”, this book summarizes the fundamental and technical changes brought by the establishment of print shops, and then focuses on how printing transformed traditional institutions and influenced three cultural movements of fundamental importance to the West: the Renaissance, the Reformation, and the rise of modern science.

271.title: TFF lifts the Arial requirement.
271.summary: The campaign launched against the Turkish Football Federation's policy mandating the use of Arial for jersey names and numbers has yielded results. Following a decision taken at the TFF Board of Directors meeting dated July 31, 2025 (numbered 48), the Sporting Equipment Directive was amended, and the requirement to…
271.content:
The campaign launched against the Turkish Football Federation's policy mandating the use of Arial for jersey names and numbers has yielded results. Following a decision taken at the TFF Board of Directors meeting dated July 31, 2025 (numbered 48), the [Sporting Equipment Directive](https://www.tff.org/Resources/TFF/Documents/TALIMATLAR/Sportif-Ekipman-Talimati.pdf) was amended, and the requirement to use Arial on jerseys was [lifted](https://x.com/TFF_Org/status/1950933292787576987). Consequently, football clubs will be able to use any typeface they wish on their jerseys, provided that it meets legibility criteria and receives approval from the TFF. In addition, typeface changes may also be made after the season begins, in accordance with the conditions specified in the directive.

While the new regulation grants clubs greater design freedom, it also brings along some practical uncertainties. Although Article 4 of the directive states, “It is essential that the numbers and names used be in an easily legible typeface on the back of the jersey,” the lack of clarification regarding which criteria legibility will be evaluated against and what expertise the decision-makers will hold raises questions.

As you may recall, in the [article](https://medium.com/tipografi/sahadaki-harfler-spor-markalamas%C4%B1nda-tipografinin-y%C3%BCkselen-g%C3%BCc%C3%BC-8f249d1300ad) we published in early July, we highlighted the rising power of typography in sports branding and examined examples of how clubs worldwide strengthen their identities through custom typefaces. This decision taken by the TFF can be regarded as an important step toward developing the visual identities of local clubs. However, time will tell whether this freedom will yield creative and high-quality results, as seen in international examples.

273.content:
American type designer [Jim Parkinson](https://typedesign.com/About.html) [passed away](https://typographica.org/on-typography/jim-parkinson-1941-2025/) on June 26, 2025, at the age of 83. Best known for designing the iconic logo of Rolling Stone magazine, Parkinson produced dozens of works over a career spanning more than fifty years, ranging from type designs to publications such as Esquire and the Los Angeles Times, as well as musical acts like the Doobie Brothers. Parkinson, who passed away due to complications from Alzheimer’s disease, left behind an enduring typographic legacy.

[Font Licensing Mess](https://fontlicensingmess.com/), an independent research project conducted by María Ramos and Ana Moliz, aims to guide interested parties by examining the complex and ambiguous world of font licenses through clarity, structure, and a data-driven approach. 277.content:
> “When you examine a typeface designed by someone else, you do a kind of forensic or archaeological work. It’s a great pleasure to explore what exists, enhance it from a new perspective, and turn it into an even more versatile type family.” Maria Doreuli

In the [bulletin](https://medium.com/tipografi/tipografi-b%C3%BClteni-aral%C4%B1k-2024-b5fc8e46b4ce) we published in December 2024, we shared [TikTok Sans](https://www.grillitype.com/commissions/tiktok-custom-font), the custom typeface Grilli Type designed for TikTok. Now, there is a significant development regarding this typeface: as a result of a collaboration led by Type Network, TikTok Sans has been made available to everyone via [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/TikTok+Sans) in an open-source and expanded version.

The typeface developed by TikTok with Grilli Type was transformed into a multi-axis type system with contributions from Type Network, Contrast Foundry, and Aaron Bell. It has now become a typeface that anyone—not just a single brand—can freely use and build upon.

281.title: Artificial intelligence and the future of typography
281.summary: “The future of typography is uncertain!” Geoffrey Bunting penned an article discussing the potential impacts of artificial intelligence on typography, drawing from Monotype’s “Re:Vision” report, which we featured in our March 2025 bulletin. According to Bunting, artificial intelligence could democratize type design by…
281.content:
> “The future of typography is uncertain!”

Geoffrey Bunting penned an [article](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/688637/typography-fonts-ai) discussing the potential impacts of artificial intelligence on typography, drawing from Monotype’s “[Re:Vision](https://www.monotype.com/type-trends)” report, which we featured in our [March 2025 bulletin](https://medium.com/tipografi/tipografi-b%C3%BClteni-mart-2025-09e6ff1f9a12). According to Bunting, artificial intelligence could democratize type design by opening it to broader audiences, but this could also bring ethical questions such as the loss of creative control to the fore. Noting that some experts compare these developments to the industrial transformations of the early twentieth century, Bunting anticipates that realistic applications are still limited, yet AI could make significant contributions to multilingual writing systems.

291.title: Finally
291.summary: Founded in 2010, our community—though having taken breaks from time to time—has continued to contribute to our typography culture through articles, interviews, and newsletters regularly since 2019. Every month, with every issue, we wonder who we have reached—which line resonated with whom and where. We are interested…
291.content:
Founded in 2010, our community—though having taken breaks from time to time—has continued to contribute to our typography culture through articles, interviews, and newsletters regularly since 2019. Every month, with every issue, we wonder who we have reached—which line resonated with whom and where. We are interested in voices, not statistics. That is why even a brief hello, a thank you, a few words of feedback, or simply saying “[I'm here](mailto:tipografitoplulugu@gmail.com)” means a great deal to us.

**See you in the next bulletin!**
